<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

1	# dog
2	
3	**dog** is a command-line DNS client, like `dig`.
4	
5	It has colourful output, understands normal command-line argument syntax, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.
6	
7	![A screenshot of dog making a DNS request](dog-screenshot.png)
8	
9	## Examples
10	
11	    dog example.net                          Query a domain using default settings
12	    dog example.net MX                       ...looking up MX records instead
13	    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1              ...using a specific nameserver instead
14	    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T           ...using TCP rather than UDP
15	    dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T   As above, but using explicit arguments
16	
17	## Command-line options
18	
19	### Query options
20	
21	    <arguments>              Human-readable host names, nameservers, types, or classes
22	    -q, --query=HOST         Host name or domain name to query
23	    -t, --type=TYPE          Type of the DNS record being queried (A, MX, NS...)
24	    -n, --nameserver=ADDR    Address of the nameserver to send packets to
25	    --class=CLASS            Network class of the DNS record being queried (IN, CH, HS)
26	
27	### Sending options
28	
29	    --edns=SETTING           Whether to OPT in to EDNS (disable, hide, show)
30	    --txid=NUMBER            Set the transaction ID to a specific value
31	    -Z=TWEAKS                Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks
32	
33	### Protocol options
34	
35	    -U, --udp                Use the DNS protocol over UDP
36	    -T, --tcp                Use the DNS protocol over TCP
37	    -S, --tls                Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol
38	    -H, --https              Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol
39	
40	### Output options
41	
42	    -1, --short              Short mode: display nothing but the first result
43	    -J, --json               Display the output as JSON
44	    --color, --colour=WHEN   When to colourise the output (always, automatic, never)

1	% dog(1) v0.1.0
2	
3	<!-- This is the dog(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->
4	<!-- To generate the roff version, run `just man`, -->
5	<!-- and the man page will appear in the ‘target’ directory. -->
6	
7	
8	NAME
9	====
10	
11	dog — a command-line DNS client
12	
13	
14	SYNOPSIS
15	========
16	
17	`dog [options] [domains...]`
18	
19	**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
20	It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.
21	
22	
23	EXAMPLES
24	========
25	
26	`dog example.net`
27	: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings
28	
29	`dog example.net MX`
30	: ...looking up `MX` records instead
31	
32	`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
33	: ...using a specific nameserver instead
34	
35	`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
36	: ...using TCP rather than UDP
37	
38	`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
39	: As above, but using explicit arguments
40	
41	
42	QUERY OPTIONS
43	=============
44	
45	`-q`, `--query=HOST`
46	: Host name or domain name to query.
47	
48	`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
49	: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)
50	
51	`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
52	: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.
53	
54	`--class=CLASS`
55	: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)
56	
57	By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.
58	
59	Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.
60	
61	If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.
62	
63	DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.
64	
65	
66	SENDING OPTIONS
67	===============
68	
69	`--edns=SETTING`
70	: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.
71	
72	`--txid=NUMBER`
73	: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.
74	
75	`-Z=TWEAKS`
76	: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.
77	
78	
79	TRANSPORT OPTIONS
80	=================
81	
82	`-U`, `--udp`
83	: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.
84	
85	`-T`, `--tcp`
86	: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.
87	
88	`-S`, `--tls`
89	: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.
90	
91	`-H`, `--https`
92	: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.
93	
94	By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.
95	
96	The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.
97	
98	Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.
99	
100	Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.
101	
102	
103	OUTPUT OPTIONS
104	==============
105	
106	`-1`, `--short`
107	: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.
108	
109	`-J`, `--json`
110	: Display the output as JSON.
111	
112	`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`
113	: When to colourise the output. This can be ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’, or ‘`never`’.
114	
115	`--seconds`
116	: Do not format durations as hours and minutes; instead, display them as seconds.
117	
118	`--time`
119	: Print how long the response took to arrive.
120	
121	
122	META OPTIONS
123	============
124	
125	`--help`
126	: Displays an overview of the command-line options.
127	
128	`--version`
129	: Displays the version of dog being invoked.
130	
131	
132	ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
133	=====================
134	
135	dog responds to the following environment variables:
136	
137	## `DOG_DEBUG`
138	
139	Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.
140	
141	
142	RECORD TYPES
143	============
144	
145	dog understands and can interpret the following record types:
146	
147	`A`
148	: IPv4 addresses
149	
150	`AAAA`
151	: IPv6 addresses
152	
153	`CAA`
154	: permitted certificate authorities
155	
156	`CNAME`
157	: canonical domain aliases
158	
159	`HINFO`
160	: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations
161	
162	`LOC`
163	: location information
164	
165	`MX`
166	: e-mail server addresses
167	
168	`NAPTR`
169	: DDDS rules
170	
171	`NS`
172	: domain name servers
173	
174	`OPT`
175	: extensions to the DNS protocol
176	
177	`PTR`
178	: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups
179	
180	`SOA`
181	: administrative information about zones
182	
183	`SRV`
184	: IP addresses with port numbers
185	
186	`SSHFP`
187	: SSH key fingerprints
188	
189	`TLSA`
190	: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes
191	
192	`TXT`
193	: arbitrary textual information
194	
195	When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.
196	
197	Records with a type number that does not map to any known record type will still be displayed. As they cannot be interpreted, their contents will be displayed as a series of numbers instead.
198	
199	dog also contains a list of record type names that it knows the type number of, but is not able to interpret, such as `IXFR` or `ANY` or `AFSDB`. These are acceptable as command-line arguments, meaning you can send an AFSDB request with ‘`dog AFSDB`’. However, their response contents will still be displayed as numbers. They may be supported in future versions of dog.
200	
201	
202	PROTOCOL TWEAKS
203	===============
204	
205	The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:
206	
207	`aa`
208	: Sets the `AA` (Authoritative Answers) bit in the query.
209	
210	`ad`
211	: Sets the `AD` (Authentic Data) bit in the query.
212	
213	`bufsize=NUM`
214	: Sets the UDP payload size field in the OPT field in the query. This has no effect if EDNS is diabled.
215	
216	`cd`
217	: Sets the `CD` (Checking Disabled) bit in the query.
218	
219	
220	EXIT STATUSES
221	=============
222	
223	0
224	: If everything goes OK.
225	
226	1
227	: If there was a network, I/O, or TLS error during operation.
228	
229	2
230	: If there is no result from the server when running in short mode. This can be any received server error, not just NXDOMAIN.
231	
232	3
233	: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.
234	
235	4
236	: If there was a problem obtaining the system nameserver information.
237	
238	
239	AUTHOR
240	======
241	
242	dog is maintained by Benjamin ‘ogham’ Sago.
243	
244	**Website:** `https://dns.lookup.dog/` \
245	**Source code:** `https://github.com/ogham/dog`

# Briefing: probing the `dog` binary

You are helping reimplement a compiled binary from observed behavior (clean-room
reverse-engineering benchmark). The binary is `/workspace/executable` — it is
`dog`, a command-line DNS client (like `dig`). Your job: run it, observe, and
write a precise behavior spec. DO NOT write implementation code.

## HARD RULES (violations disqualify the whole project)

- ONLY interact with `/workspace/executable` through its normal CLI
  (arguments, stdin/stdout, environment variables).
- NEVER run `strings`, `objdump`, `readelf`, `nm`, `gdb`, `strace`, `ltrace`
  or any disassembler/tracer on it. Do not inspect its bytes at all.
- No internet access (there is none anyway). Do not look up the dog project.
- Do not install anything.

## Environment

- Working dir: `/workspace`. Docs: `README.md`, `man/dog.1.md`, `completions/`.
- There is NO external network. To observe query/response behavior, run a fake
  DNS server on 127.0.0.1 using the toolkit at `/workspace/probe/dnskit.py`
  (read it first). Examples: `/workspace/probe/smoke.py`, `/workspace/probe/misc.py`.
- Pattern for a probe (self-contained, no leftover servers):

  ```bash
  cd /workspace && python3 probe/myprobe.py <PORT> >/tmp/mylog 2>&1 & SRV=$!
  sleep 0.4
  timeout 10 ./executable example.com @127.0.0.1:<PORT> | cat -v
  echo "EXIT: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
  kill $SRV 2>/dev/null
  ```

  ALWAYS use `timeout 10` when invoking the executable (it can hang waiting
  for network). Use your assigned port range only — other agents run in parallel.
- `cat -v` reveals ANSI escape codes (`^[[1;32m` etc). To see exact spacing
  use `cat -A` (shows `$` at line end). Record outputs EXACTLY, byte for byte.
- `DOG_DEBUG=1` / `DOG_DEBUG=trace` env vars make it log to stderr — useful
  for understanding internal behavior (allowed: it is a documented UI feature).

## dnskit quick reference

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

def handler(q):                      # q = raw query bytes
    r = Response(q)                  # copies txid + question section
    # kwargs: qr, opcode, aa, tc, rd, ra, z, ad, cd, rcode (int)
    r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))        # (name, type, ttl, rdata, rrclass="IN")
    r.add_authority("example.com", "NS", 3600, name("ns1.example.com"))
    r.add_additional("x.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT("hello", "world"))
    r.add_answer_raw("example.com", 99, 1, 60, b"\x01\x02")    # raw type/class ints
    return r                         # auto-built by serve()

def on_query(parsed, raw): print(parsed, raw.hex(), flush=True)  # see what dog sent

serve(handler, port=PORT)            # UDP+TCP on 127.0.0.1 forever
```

rdata helpers: `name()`, `A()`, `AAAA()`, `MX()`, `TXT()`, `SOA()`, `SRV()`,
`CAA()`, `HINFO()`, `SSHFP()`, `TLSA()`, `NAPTR()`, `LOC()`, `OPT()`, `raw(hex)`.
Write your own probe scripts under `/workspace/probe/<area>_*.py`.

## Known basics (already observed)

- `dog example.com @127.0.0.1:PORT` → `A example.com. 5m00s   93.184.216.34` (exit 0)
- Default query: RD flag set, EDNS OPT record with UDP payload 512, random txid.
- NXDOMAIN response → prints `Status: NXDomain`, exit 0.
- Unknown rtype 99 renders as `99 example.com. 1m00s   [1, 2, 3, 4]`.
- Authority records render like `NS example.com. 1h00m00s A "ns1.example.com."`,
  additionals like ` A ns1.example.com. 1h00m00s + 5.6.7.8`.
- TTLs are formatted as durations (`5m00s`, `1h00m00s`).
- Columns are aligned (type right-aligned, name left-aligned, TTL right-aligned).
- `-J` JSON: `{"responses":[{"queries":[...],"answers":[{"name":..,"class":..,"ttl":..,"type":..,"data":{...}}],"authorities":[],"additionals":[]}]}`
- `-1` short: prints just the first rdata. `--time`: appends `Ran in 0ms` line.
- Colors with `--color=always`: `A` is bold green (1;32), name is bold blue (1;34).
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 network error, 2 short-mode no result, 3 bad args, 4 resolver problem.

## What to deliver

Write your spec to `/workspace/specs/<your-area>.md`. It must be precise enough
that a programmer can reproduce byte-identical output without ever seeing the
binary: exact strings, exact spacing, exact ANSI codes, exact exit codes,
exact wire bytes, and the exact commands/scenarios you used. Note anything
surprising. Organize by scenario with example invocations and outputs.

1	"""Minimal DNS wire-format toolkit for probing the dog binary.
2	
3	Build DNS response packets by hand and serve them over UDP/TCP so we can
4	observe exactly how `./executable` renders them.
5	
6	Usage pattern in a probe script:
7	
8	    from dnskit import *
9	    def handler(query_bytes, txn):
10	        resp = Response(txn)  # copies id, flags, question
11	        resp.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
12	        return resp.build()
13	    serve(handler, port=5353)   # UDP+TCP forever
14	"""
15	
16	import socket
17	import struct
18	import threading
19	
20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- builders
21	
22	TYPE_CODES = {
23	    "A": 1, "NS": 2, "CNAME": 5, "SOA": 6, "PTR": 12, "HINFO": 13,
24	    "MX": 15, "TXT": 16, "AAAA": 28, "LOC": 29, "SRV": 33, "NAPTR": 35,
25	    "OPT": 41, "SSHFP": 44, "TLSA": 52, "CAA": 257,
26	}
27	CLASS_CODES = {"IN": 1, "CH": 3, "HS": 4}
28	
29	RCODES = {"NOERROR": 0, "FORMERR": 1, "SERVFAIL": 2, "NXDOMAIN": 3,
30	          "NOTIMP": 4, "REFUSED": 5}
31	
32	
33	def name(s):
34	    """Encode a domain name to wire format."""
35	    if s == "." or s == "":
36	        return b"\x00"
37	    out = b""
38	    for part in s.rstrip(".").split("."):
39	        out += bytes([len(part)]) + part.encode()
40	    return out + b"\x00"
41	
42	
43	def A(ip):
44	    return socket.inet_aton(ip)
45	
46	
47	def AAAA(ip6):
48	    return socket.inet_pton(socket.AF_INET6, ip6)
49	
50	
51	def MX(pref, host):
52	    return struct.pack(">H", pref) + name(host)
53	
54	
55	def TXT(*strings):
56	    out = b""
57	    for s in strings:
58	        b = s.encode() if isinstance(s, str) else s
59	        out += bytes([len(b)]) + b
60	    return out
61	
62	
63	def SOA(mname, rname, serial, refresh, retry, expire, minimum):
64	    return (name(mname) + name(rname) +
65	            struct.pack(">IIIII", serial, refresh, retry, expire, minimum))
66	
67	
68	def SRV(prio, weight, port, target):
69	    return struct.pack(">HHH", prio, weight, port) + name(target)
70	
71	
72	def CAA(flags, tag, value):
73	    tb = tag.encode()
74	    vb = value.encode() if isinstance(value, str) else value
75	    return bytes([flags, len(tb)]) + tb + vb
76	
77	
78	def HINFO(cpu, os_):
79	    return TXT(cpu, os_)
80	
81	
82	def SSHFP(alg, fptype, fp_hex):
83	    return bytes([alg, fptype]) + bytes.fromhex(fp_hex)
84	
85	
86	def TLSA(usage, selector, mtype, data_hex):
87	    return bytes([usage, selector, mtype]) + bytes.fromhex(data_hex)
88	
89	
90	def NAPTR(order, pref, flags, service, regexp, replacement):
91	    out = struct.pack(">HH", order, pref)
92	    for s in (flags, service, regexp):
93	        b = s.encode()
94	        out += bytes([len(b)]) + b
95	    return out + name(replacement)
96	
97	
98	def LOC(version, size, hp, vp, lat, lon, alt):
99	    return struct.pack(">BBBBIII", version, size, hp, vp, lat, lon, alt)
100	
101	
102	def OPT(payload_size, ext_rcode, version, flags, options=b""):
103	    return struct.pack(">HBBH", payload_size, ext_rcode, version, flags) + options
104	
105	
106	def raw(hexstr):
107	    return bytes.fromhex(hexstr)
108	
109	
110	class Response:
111	    def __init__(self, query_bytes=None, txid=0x1234, qr=1, opcode=0, aa=0,
112	                 tc=0, rd=1, ra=1, z=0, ad=0, cd=0, rcode=0):
113	        self.txid = txid
114	        self.flags = ((qr << 15) | (opcode << 11) | (aa << 10) | (tc << 9) |
115	                      (rd << 8) | (ra << 7) | (z << 6) | (ad << 5) |
116	                      (cd << 4) | rcode)
117	        self.questions = []
118	        self.answers = []
119	        self.authorities = []
120	        self.additionals = []
121	        if query_bytes is not None:
122	            self.txid = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[:2])[0]
123	            qd = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[4:6])[0]
124	            # copy question section verbatim
125	            off = 12
126	            self._qraw = b""
127	            for _ in range(qd):
128	                start = off
129	                while query_bytes[off] != 0:
130	                    off += 1 + query_bytes[off]
131	                off += 5  # null + type + class
132	                self._qraw += query_bytes[start:off]
133	            self.qdcount = qd
134	        else:
135	            self._qraw = b""
136	            self.qdcount = 0
137	
138	    def add_question(self, qname, qtype="A", qclass="IN"):
139	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(qtype, qtype if isinstance(qtype, int) else 1)
140	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(qclass, qclass if isinstance(qclass, int) else 1)
141	        self._qraw += name(qname) + struct.pack(">HH", t, c)
142	        self.qdcount += 1
143	
144	    def _record(self, section, rname_, rtype, ttl, rdata, rrclass="IN"):
145	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(rtype, rtype if isinstance(rtype, int) else 1)
146	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(rrclass, rrclass if isinstance(rrclass, int) else 1)
147	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", t, c, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
148	        section.append(rec)
149	
150	    def add_answer(self, *a):
151	        self._record(self.answers, *a)
152	
153	    def add_authority(self, *a):
154	        self._record(self.authorities, *a)
155	
156	    def add_additional(self, *a):
157	        self._record(self.additionals, *a)
158	
159	    def add_answer_raw(self, rname_, rtype, rrclass, ttl, rdata):
160	        """rtype/rrclass as raw integers (for unknown types/classes)."""
161	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", rtype, rrclass, ttl,
162	                                         len(rdata)) + rdata
163	        self.answers.append(rec)
164	
165	    def build(self):
166	        hdr = struct.pack(">HHHHHH", self.txid, self.flags, self.qdcount,
167	                          len(self.answers), len(self.authorities),
168	                          len(self.additionals))
169	        return (hdr + self._qraw + b"".join(self.answers) +
170	                b"".join(self.authorities) + b"".join(self.additionals))
171	
172	
173	def parse_query(data):
174	    """Return dict describing a query packet (for logging what dog sent)."""
175	    txid, flags, qd, an, ns, ar = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[:12])
176	    off = 12
177	    questions = []
178	    for _ in range(qd):
179	        labels = []
180	        while data[off] != 0:
181	            n = data[off]
182	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode("ascii", "replace"))
183	            off += 1 + n
184	        off += 1
185	        qtype, qclass = struct.unpack(">HH", data[off:off + 4])
186	        off += 4
187	        questions.append((".".join(labels), qtype, qclass))
188	    additionals = []
189	    for _ in range(ar):
190	        labels = []
191	        while data[off] != 0:
192	            if data[off] & 0xC0 == 0xC0:
193	                off += 2
194	                break
195	            n = data[off]
196	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode())
197	            off += 1 + n
198	        else:
199	            off += 1
200	        rtype, rclass, ttl, rdlen = struct.unpack(">HHIH", data[off:off + 10])
201	        off += 10
202	        additionals.append((".".join(labels), rtype, rclass, ttl,
203	                            data[off:off + rdlen].hex()))
204	        off += rdlen
205	    return {"txid": txid, "flags": flags, "qd": qd, "an": an, "ar": ar,
206	            "questions": questions, "additionals": additionals}
207	
208	
209	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- server
210	
211	def serve(handler, port=5353, tcp=True, udp=True, log=True, on_query=None):
212	    """Serve DNS over UDP and TCP. handler(query_bytes) -> response bytes
213	    (or None to not respond). on_query(parsed_dict, raw) called per query."""
214	    socks = []
215	    if udp:
216	        u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
217	        u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
218	        u.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
219	        socks.append(("udp", u))
220	    if tcp:
221	        t = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
222	        t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
223	        t.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
224	        t.listen(5)
225	        socks.append(("tcp", t))
226	
227	    def loop(proto, s):
228	        while True:
229	            try:
230	                if proto == "udp":
231	                    data, addr = s.recvfrom(65535)
232	                    if on_query:
233	                        on_query(parse_query(data), data)
234	                    resp = handler(data)
235	                    if isinstance(resp, Response):
236	                        resp = resp.build()
237	                    if resp is not None:
238	                        s.sendto(resp, addr)
239	                else:
240	                    conn, _ = s.accept()
241	                    threading.Thread(target=tcp_conn,
242	                                     args=(conn, handler, on_query),
243	                                     daemon=True).start()
244	            except Exception as e:
245	                if log:
246	                    print(f"[{proto} error] {e}", flush=True)
247	
248	    def tcp_conn(conn, handler, on_query):
249	        try:
250	            while True:
251	                hdr = recv_exact(conn, 2)
252	                if not hdr:
253	                    break
254	                (length,) = struct.unpack(">H", hdr)
255	                data = recv_exact(conn, length)
256	                if on_query:
257	                    on_query(parse_query(data), data)
258	                resp = handler(data)
259	                if isinstance(resp, Response):
260	                    resp = resp.build()
261	                if resp is not None:
262	                    conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(resp)) + resp)
263	        except Exception:
264	            pass
265	        finally:
266	            conn.close()
267	
268	    for proto, s in socks:
269	        threading.Thread(target=loop, args=(proto, s), daemon=True).start()
270	    print(f"serving on 127.0.0.1:{port}", flush=True)
271	    threading.Event().wait()
272	
273	
274	def recv_exact(conn, n):
275	    buf = b""
276	    while len(buf) < n:
277	        chunk = conn.recv(n - len(buf))
278	        if not chunk:
279	            return None
280	        buf += chunk
281	    return buf

3	<!-- This is the dog(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->

6	
7	
8	NAME
9	====
10	
11	dog — a command-line DNS client
12	
13	
14	SYNOPSIS
15	========
16	
17	`dog [options] [domains...]`
18	
19	**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
20	It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.
21	
22	
23	EXAMPLES
24	========
25	
26	`dog example.net`
27	: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings
28	
29	`dog example.net MX`
30	: ...looking up `MX` records instead
31	
32	`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
33	: ...using a specific nameserver instead
34	
35	`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
36	: ...using TCP rather than UDP
37	
38	`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
39	: As above, but using explicit arguments
40	
41	
42	QUERY OPTIONS
43	=============
44	
45	`-q`, `--query=HOST`
46	: Host name or domain name to query.
47	
48	`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
49	: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)
50	
51	`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
52	: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.
53	
54	`--class=CLASS`
55	: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)
56	
57	By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.
58	
59	Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.
60	
61	If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.
62	
63	DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.
64	
65	
66	SENDING OPTIONS
67	===============
68	
69	`--edns=SETTING`
70	: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.
71	
72	`--txid=NUMBER`
73	: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.
74	
75	`-Z=TWEAKS`
76	: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.
77	
78	
79	TRANSPORT OPTIONS
80	=================
81	
82	`-U`, `--udp`
83	: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.
84	
85	`-T`, `--tcp`
86	: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.
87	
88	`-S`, `--tls`
89	: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.
90	
91	`-H`, `--https`
92	: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.
93	
94	By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.
95	
96	The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.
97	
98	Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.
99	
100	Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.
101	
102	
103	OUTPUT OPTIONS
104	==============
105	
106	`-1`, `--short`
107	: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.
108	
109	`-J`, `--json`
110	: Display the output as JSON.
111	
112	`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`
113	: When to colourise the output. This can be ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’, or ‘`never`’.
114	
115	`--seconds`
116	: Do not format durations as hours and minutes; instead, display them as seconds.
117	
118	`--time`
119	: Print how long the response took to arrive.
120	
121	
122	META OPTIONS
123	============
124	
125	`--help`
126	: Displays an overview of the command-line options.
127	
128	`--version`
129	: Displays the version of dog being invoked.
130	
131	
132	ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
133	=====================
134	
135	dog responds to the following environment variables:
136	
137	## `DOG_DEBUG`
138	
139	Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.
140	
141	
142	RECORD TYPES
143	============
144	
145	dog understands and can interpret the following record types:
146	
147	`A`
148	: IPv4 addresses
149	
150	`AAAA`
151	: IPv6 addresses
152	
153	`CAA`
154	: permitted certificate authorities
155	
156	`CNAME`
157	: canonical domain aliases
158	
159	`HINFO`
160	: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations
161	
162	`LOC`
163	: location information
164	
165	`MX`
166	: e-mail server addresses
167	
168	`NAPTR`
169	: DDDS rules
170	
171	`NS`
172	: domain name servers
173	
174	`OPT`
175	: extensions to the DNS protocol
176	
177	`PTR`
178	: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups
179	
180	`SOA`
181	: administrative information about zones
182	
183	`SRV`
184	: IP addresses with port numbers
185	
186	`SSHFP`
187	: SSH key fingerprints
188	
189	`TLSA`
190	: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes
191	
192	`TXT`
193	: arbitrary textual information
194	
195	When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.
196	
197	Records with a type number that does not map to any known record type will still be displayed. As they cannot be interpreted, their contents will be displayed as a series of numbers instead.
198	
199	dog also contains a list of record type names that it knows the type number of, but is not able to interpret, such as `IXFR` or `ANY` or `AFSDB`. These are acceptable as command-line arguments, meaning you can send an AFSDB request with ‘`dog AFSDB`’. However, their response contents will still be displayed as numbers. They may be supported in future versions of dog.
200	
201	
202	PROTOCOL TWEAKS
203	===============
204	
205	The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:
206	
207	`aa`
208	: Sets the `AA` (Authoritative Answers) bit in the query.
209	
210	`ad`
211	: Sets the `AD` (Authentic Data) bit in the query.
212	
213	`bufsize=NUM`
214	: Sets the UDP payload size field in the OPT field in the query. This has no effect if EDNS is diabled.
215	
216	`cd`
217	: Sets the `CD` (Checking Disabled) bit in the query.
218	
219	
220	EXIT STATUSES
221	=============
222	
223	0
224	: If everything goes OK.
225	
226	1
227	: If there was a network, I/O, or TLS error during operation.
228	
229	2
230	: If there is no result from the server when running in short mode. This can be any received server error, not just NXDOMAIN.
231	
232	3
233	: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.
234	
235	4
236	: If there was a problem obtaining the system nameserver information.
237	
238	
239	AUTHOR
240	======
241	
242	dog is maintained by Benjamin ‘ogham’ Sago.
243	
244	**Website:** `https://dns.lookup.dog/` \
245	**Source code:** `https://github.com/ogham/dog`

1	"""Minimal DNS wire-format toolkit for probing the dog binary.
2	
3	Build DNS response packets by hand and serve them over UDP/TCP so we can
4	observe exactly how `./executable` renders them.
5	
6	Usage pattern in a probe script:
7	
8	    from dnskit import *
9	    def handler(query_bytes, txn):
10	        resp = Response(txn)  # copies id, flags, question
11	        resp.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
12	        return resp.build()
13	    serve(handler, port=5353)   # UDP+TCP forever
14	"""
15	
16	import socket
17	import struct
18	import threading
19	
20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- builders
21	
22	TYPE_CODES = {
23	    "A": 1, "NS": 2, "CNAME": 5, "SOA": 6, "PTR": 12, "HINFO": 13,
24	    "MX": 15, "TXT": 16, "AAAA": 28, "LOC": 29, "SRV": 33, "NAPTR": 35,
25	    "OPT": 41, "SSHFP": 44, "TLSA": 52, "CAA": 257,
26	}
27	CLASS_CODES = {"IN": 1, "CH": 3, "HS": 4}
28	
29	RCODES = {"NOERROR": 0, "FORMERR": 1, "SERVFAIL": 2, "NXDOMAIN": 3,
30	          "NOTIMP": 4, "REFUSED": 5}
31	
32	
33	def name(s):
34	    """Encode a domain name to wire format."""
35	    if s == "." or s == "":
36	        return b"\x00"
37	    out = b""
38	    for part in s.rstrip(".").split("."):
39	        out += bytes([len(part)]) + part.encode()
40	    return out + b"\x00"
41	
42	
43	def A(ip):
44	    return socket.inet_aton(ip)
45	
46	
47	def AAAA(ip6):
48	    return socket.inet_pton(socket.AF_INET6, ip6)
49	
50	
51	def MX(pref, host):
52	    return struct.pack(">H", pref) + name(host)
53	
54	
55	def TXT(*strings):
56	    out = b""
57	    for s in strings:
58	        b = s.encode() if isinstance(s, str) else s
59	        out += bytes([len(b)]) + b
60	    return out
61	
62	
63	def SOA(mname, rname, serial, refresh, retry, expire, minimum):
64	    return (name(mname) + name(rname) +
65	            struct.pack(">IIIII", serial, refresh, retry, expire, minimum))
66	
67	
68	def SRV(prio, weight, port, target):
69	    return struct.pack(">HHH", prio, weight, port) + name(target)
70	
71	
72	def CAA(flags, tag, value):
73	    tb = tag.encode()
74	    vb = value.encode() if isinstance(value, str) else value
75	    return bytes([flags, len(tb)]) + tb + vb
76	
77	
78	def HINFO(cpu, os_):
79	    return TXT(cpu, os_)
80	
81	
82	def SSHFP(alg, fptype, fp_hex):
83	    return bytes([alg, fptype]) + bytes.fromhex(fp_hex)
84	
85	
86	def TLSA(usage, selector, mtype, data_hex):
87	    return bytes([usage, selector, mtype]) + bytes.fromhex(data_hex)
88	
89	
90	def NAPTR(order, pref, flags, service, regexp, replacement):
91	    out = struct.pack(">HH", order, pref)
92	    for s in (flags, service, regexp):
93	        b = s.encode()
94	        out += bytes([len(b)]) + b
95	    return out + name(replacement)
96	
97	
98	def LOC(version, size, hp, vp, lat, lon, alt):
99	    return struct.pack(">BBBBIII", version, size, hp, vp, lat, lon, alt)
100	
101	
102	def OPT(payload_size, ext_rcode, version, flags, options=b""):
103	    return struct.pack(">HBBH", payload_size, ext_rcode, version, flags) + options
104	
105	
106	def raw(hexstr):
107	    return bytes.fromhex(hexstr)
108	
109	
110	class Response:
111	    def __init__(self, query_bytes=None, txid=0x1234, qr=1, opcode=0, aa=0,
112	                 tc=0, rd=1, ra=1, z=0, ad=0, cd=0, rcode=0):
113	        self.txid = txid
114	        self.flags = ((qr << 15) | (opcode << 11) | (aa << 10) | (tc << 9) |
115	                      (rd << 8) | (ra << 7) | (z << 6) | (ad << 5) |
116	                      (cd << 4) | rcode)
117	        self.questions = []
118	        self.answers = []
119	        self.authorities = []
120	        self.additionals = []
121	        if query_bytes is not None:
122	            self.txid = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[:2])[0]
123	            qd = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[4:6])[0]
124	            # copy question section verbatim
125	            off = 12
126	            self._qraw = b""
127	            for _ in range(qd):
128	                start = off
129	                while query_bytes[off] != 0:
130	                    off += 1 + query_bytes[off]
131	                off += 5  # null + type + class
132	                self._qraw += query_bytes[start:off]
133	            self.qdcount = qd
134	        else:
135	            self._qraw = b""
136	            self.qdcount = 0
137	
138	    def add_question(self, qname, qtype="A", qclass="IN"):
139	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(qtype, qtype if isinstance(qtype, int) else 1)
140	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(qclass, qclass if isinstance(qclass, int) else 1)
141	        self._qraw += name(qname) + struct.pack(">HH", t, c)
142	        self.qdcount += 1
143	
144	    def _record(self, section, rname_, rtype, ttl, rdata, rrclass="IN"):
145	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(rtype, rtype if isinstance(rtype, int) else 1)
146	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(rrclass, rrclass if isinstance(rrclass, int) else 1)
147	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", t, c, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
148	        section.append(rec)
149	
150	    def add_answer(self, *a):
151	        self._record(self.answers, *a)
152	
153	    def add_authority(self, *a):
154	        self._record(self.authorities, *a)
155	
156	    def add_additional(self, *a):
157	        self._record(self.additionals, *a)
158	
159	    def add_answer_raw(self, rname_, rtype, rrclass, ttl, rdata):
160	        """rtype/rrclass as raw integers (for unknown types/classes)."""
161	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", rtype, rrclass, ttl,
162	                                         len(rdata)) + rdata
163	        self.answers.append(rec)
164	
165	    def build(self):
166	        hdr = struct.pack(">HHHHHH", self.txid, self.flags, self.qdcount,
167	                          len(self.answers), len(self.authorities),
168	                          len(self.additionals))
169	        return (hdr + self._qraw + b"".join(self.answers) +
170	                b"".join(self.authorities) + b"".join(self.additionals))
171	
172	
173	def parse_query(data):
174	    """Return dict describing a query packet (for logging what dog sent)."""
175	    txid, flags, qd, an, ns, ar = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[:12])
176	    off = 12
177	    questions = []
178	    for _ in range(qd):
179	        labels = []
180	        while data[off] != 0:
181	            n = data[off]
182	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode("ascii", "replace"))
183	            off += 1 + n
184	        off += 1
185	        qtype, qclass = struct.unpack(">HH", data[off:off + 4])
186	        off += 4
187	        questions.append((".".join(labels), qtype, qclass))
188	    additionals = []
189	    for _ in range(ar):
190	        labels = []
191	        while data[off] != 0:
192	            if data[off] & 0xC0 == 0xC0:
193	                off += 2
194	                break
195	            n = data[off]
196	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode())
197	            off += 1 + n
198	        else:
199	            off += 1
200	        rtype, rclass, ttl, rdlen = struct.unpack(">HHIH", data[off:off + 10])
201	        off += 10
202	        additionals.append((".".join(labels), rtype, rclass, ttl,
203	                            data[off:off + rdlen].hex()))
204	        off += rdlen
205	    return {"txid": txid, "flags": flags, "qd": qd, "an": an, "ar": ar,
206	            "questions": questions, "additionals": additionals}
207	
208	
209	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- server
210	
211	def serve(handler, port=5353, tcp=True, udp=True, log=True, on_query=None):
212	    """Serve DNS over UDP and TCP. handler(query_bytes) -> response bytes
213	    (or None to not respond). on_query(parsed_dict, raw) called per query."""
214	    socks = []
215	    if udp:
216	        u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
217	        u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
218	        u.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
219	        socks.append(("udp", u))
220	    if tcp:
221	        t = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
222	        t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
223	        t.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
224	        t.listen(5)
225	        socks.append(("tcp", t))
226	
227	    def loop(proto, s):
228	        while True:
229	            try:
230	                if proto == "udp":
231	                    data, addr = s.recvfrom(65535)
232	                    if on_query:
233	                        on_query(parse_query(data), data)
234	                    resp = handler(data)
235	                    if isinstance(resp, Response):
236	                        resp = resp.build()
237	                    if resp is not None:
238	                        s.sendto(resp, addr)
239	                else:
240	                    conn, _ = s.accept()
241	                    threading.Thread(target=tcp_conn,
242	                                     args=(conn, handler, on_query),
243	                                     daemon=True).start()
244	            except Exception as e:
245	                if log:
246	                    print(f"[{proto} error] {e}", flush=True)
247	
248	    def tcp_conn(conn, handler, on_query):
249	        try:
250	            while True:
251	                hdr = recv_exact(conn, 2)
252	                if not hdr:
253	                    break
254	                (length,) = struct.unpack(">H", hdr)
255	                data = recv_exact(conn, length)
256	                if on_query:
257	                    on_query(parse_query(data), data)
258	                resp = handler(data)
259	                if isinstance(resp, Response):
260	                    resp = resp.build()
261	                if resp is not None:
262	                    conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(resp)) + resp)
263	        except Exception:
264	            pass
265	        finally:
266	            conn.close()
267	
268	    for proto, s in socks:
269	        threading.Thread(target=loop, args=(proto, s), daemon=True).start()
270	    print(f"serving on 127.0.0.1:{port}", flush=True)
271	    threading.Event().wait()
272	
273	
274	def recv_exact(conn, n):
275	    buf = b""
276	    while len(buf) < n:
277	        chunk = conn.recv(n - len(buf))
278	        if not chunk:
279	            return None
280	        buf += chunk
281	    return buf

QUERY OPTIONS
=============

`-q`, `--query=HOST`
: Host name or domain name to query.

`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)

`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.

`--class=CLASS`
: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)

By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.

Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.

If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.

DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.


SENDING OPTIONS
===============

`--edns=SETTING`
: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.

`--txid=NUMBER`
: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.

`-Z=TWEAKS`
: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.


TRANSPORT OPTIONS
=================

`-U`, `--udp`
: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.

`-T`, `--tcp`
: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.

`-S`, `--tls`
: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.

`-H`, `--https`
: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.

By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.

The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.

Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.

Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.
===


RECORD TYPES
============

dog understands and can interpret the following record types:

`A`
: IPv4 addresses

`AAAA`
: IPv6 addresses

`CAA`
: permitted certificate authorities

`CNAME`
: canonical domain aliases

`HINFO`
: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations

`LOC`
: location information

`MX`
: e-mail server addresses

`NAPTR`
: DDDS rules

`NS`
: domain name servers

`OPT`
: extensions to the DNS protocol

`PTR`
: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups

`SOA`
: administrative information about zones

`SRV`
: IP addresses with port numbers

`SSHFP`
: SSH key fingerprints

`TLSA`
: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes

`TXT`
: arbitrary textual information

When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.

Records with a type number that does not map to any known record type will still be displayed. As they cannot be interpreted, their contents will be displayed as a series of numbers instead.

dog also contains a list of record type names that it knows the type number of, but is not able to interpret, such as `IXFR` or `ANY` or `AFSDB`. These are acceptable as command-line arguments, meaning you can send an AFSDB request with ‘`dog AFSDB`’. However, their response contents will still be displayed as numbers. They may be supported in future versions of dog.


PROTOCOL TWEAKS
===============

The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:

`aa`
: Sets the `AA` (Authoritative Answers) bit in the query.

`ad`
: Sets the `AD` (Authentic Data) bit in the query.

`bufsize=NUM`
: Sets the UDP payload size field in the OPT field in the query. This has no effect if EDNS is diabled.

`cd`
: Sets the `CD` (Checking Disabled) bit in the query.


EXIT STATUSES
=============

0
: If everything goes OK.

1
: If there was a network, I/O, or TLS error during operation.

2
: If there is no result from the server when running in short mode. This can be any received server error, not just NXDOMAIN.

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    return r

def on_query(parsed, raw):
    import threading
    proto = "tcp" if threading.current_thread().name.startswith("Thread") else "?"
    print("QPARSED", parsed, flush=True)
    print("QHEX", raw.hex(), flush=True)

# need protocol tagging: wrap serve by monkey-level: dnskit's on_query lacks proto,
# so we run two servers on same port is impossible; instead log socket via custom.
serve(handler, port=PORT, on_query=on_query)

% dog(1) v0.1.0

<!-- This is the dog(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->
<!-- To generate the roff version, run `just man`, -->
<!-- and the man page will appear in the ‘target’ directory. -->


NAME
====

dog — a command-line DNS client


SYNOPSIS
========

`dog [options] [domains...]`

**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.


EXAMPLES
========

`dog example.net`
: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings

`dog example.net MX`
: ...looking up `MX` records instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
: ...using a specific nameserver instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
: ...using TCP rather than UDP

`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
: As above, but using explicit arguments


QUERY OPTIONS
=============

`-q`, `--query=HOST`
: Host name or domain name to query.

`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)

`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.

`--class=CLASS`
: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)

By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.

Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.

If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.

DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.


SENDING OPTIONS
===============

`--edns=SETTING`
: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.

`--txid=NUMBER`
: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.

`-Z=TWEAKS`
: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.


TRANSPORT OPTIONS
=================

`-U`, `--udp`
: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.

`-T`, `--tcp`
: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.

`-S`, `--tls`
: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.

`-H`, `--https`
: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.

By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.

The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.

Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.

Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.


OUTPUT OPTIONS
==============

`-1`, `--short`
: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.

`-J`, `--json`
: Display the output as JSON.

`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`
: When to colourise the output. This can be ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’, or ‘`never`’.

`--seconds`
: Do not format durations as hours and minutes; instead, display them as seconds.

`--time`
: Print how long the response took to arrive.


META OPTIONS
============

`--help`
: Displays an overview of the command-line options.

`--version`
: Displays the version of dog being invoked.


ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
=====================

dog responds to the following environment variables:

## `DOG_DEBUG`

Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.

2

4	observe exactly how `./executable` renders them.

8	    from dnskit import *
9	    def handler(query_bytes, txn):
10	        resp = Response(txn)  # copies id, flags, question
11	        resp.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
12	        return resp.build()
13	    serve(handler, port=5353)   # UDP+TCP forever
14	"""
15	
16	import socket
17	import struct
18	import threading
19	
20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- builders
21	
22	TYPE_CODES = {
23	    "A": 1, "NS": 2, "CNAME": 5, "SOA": 6, "PTR": 12, "HINFO": 13,
24	    "MX": 15, "TXT": 16, "AAAA": 28, "LOC": 29, "SRV": 33, "NAPTR": 35,
25	    "OPT": 41, "SSHFP": 44, "TLSA": 52, "CAA": 257,
26	}
27	CLASS_CODES = {"IN": 1, "CH": 3, "HS": 4}
28	
29	RCODES = {"NOERROR": 0, "FORMERR": 1, "SERVFAIL": 2, "NXDOMAIN": 3,
30	          "NOTIMP": 4, "REFUSED": 5}
31	
32	
33	def name(s):
34	    """Encode a domain name to wire format."""
35	    if s == "." or s == "":
36	        return b"\x00"
37	    out = b""
38	    for part in s.rstrip(".").split("."):
39	        out += bytes([len(part)]) + part.encode()
40	    return out + b"\x00"
41	
42	
43	def A(ip):
44	    return socket.inet_aton(ip)
45	
46	
47	def AAAA(ip6):
48	    return socket.inet_pton(socket.AF_INET6, ip6)
49	
50	
51	def MX(pref, host):
52	    return struct.pack(">H", pref) + name(host)
53	
54	
55	def TXT(*strings):
56	    out = b""
57	    for s in strings:
58	        b = s.encode() if isinstance(s, str) else s
59	        out += bytes([len(b)]) + b
60	    return out
61	
62	
63	def SOA(mname, rname, serial, refresh, retry, expire, minimum):
64	    return (name(mname) + name(rname) +
65	            struct.pack(">IIIII", serial, refresh, retry, expire, minimum))
66	
67	
68	def SRV(prio, weight, port, target):
69	    return struct.pack(">HHH", prio, weight, port) + name(target)
70	
71	
72	def CAA(flags, tag, value):
73	    tb = tag.encode()
74	    vb = value.encode() if isinstance(value, str) else value
75	    return bytes([flags, len(tb)]) + tb + vb
76	
77	
78	def HINFO(cpu, os_):
79	    return TXT(cpu, os_)
80	
81	
82	def SSHFP(alg, fptype, fp_hex):
83	    return bytes([alg, fptype]) + bytes.fromhex(fp_hex)
84	
85	
86	def TLSA(usage, selector, mtype, data_hex):
87	    return bytes([usage, selector, mtype]) + bytes.fromhex(data_hex)
88	
89	
90	def NAPTR(order, pref, flags, service, regexp, replacement):
91	    out = struct.pack(">HH", order, pref)
92	    for s in (flags, service, regexp):
93	        b = s.encode()
94	        out += bytes([len(b)]) + b
95	    return out + name(replacement)
96	
97	
98	def LOC(version, size, hp, vp, lat, lon, alt):
99	    return struct.pack(">BBBBIII", version, size, hp, vp, lat, lon, alt)
100	
101	
102	def OPT(payload_size, ext_rcode, version, flags, options=b""):
103	    return struct.pack(">HBBH", payload_size, ext_rcode, version, flags) + options
104	
105	
106	def raw(hexstr):
107	    return bytes.fromhex(hexstr)

110	class Response:
111	    def __init__(self, query_bytes=None, txid=0x1234, qr=1, opcode=0, aa=0,
112	                 tc=0, rd=1, ra=1, z=0, ad=0, cd=0, rcode=0):
113	        self.txid = txid
114	        self.flags = ((qr << 15) | (opcode << 11) | (aa << 10) | (tc << 9) |
115	                      (rd << 8) | (ra << 7) | (z << 6) | (ad << 5) |
116	                      (cd << 4) | rcode)
117	        self.questions = []
118	        self.answers = []
119	        self.authorities = []
120	        self.additionals = []
121	        if query_bytes is not None:
122	            self.txid = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[:2])[0]
123	            qd = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[4:6])[0]
124	            # copy question section verbatim
125	            off = 12
126	            self._qraw = b""
127	            for _ in range(qd):
128	                start = off
129	                while query_bytes[off] != 0:
130	                    off += 1 + query_bytes[off]
131	                off += 5  # null + type + class
132	                self._qraw += query_bytes[start:off]
133	            self.qdcount = qd
134	        else:
135	            self._qraw = b""
136	            self.qdcount = 0
137	
138	    def add_question(self, qname, qtype="A", qclass="IN"):
139	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(qtype, qtype if isinstance(qtype, int) else 1)
140	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(qclass, qclass if isinstance(qclass, int) else 1)
141	        self._qraw += name(qname) + struct.pack(">HH", t, c)
142	        self.qdcount += 1
143	
144	    def _record(self, section, rname_, rtype, ttl, rdata, rrclass="IN"):
145	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(rtype, rtype if isinstance(rtype, int) else 1)
146	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(rrclass, rrclass if isinstance(rrclass, int) else 1)
147	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", t, c, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
148	        section.append(rec)
149	
150	    def add_answer(self, *a):
151	        self._record(self.answers, *a)
152	
153	    def add_authority(self, *a):
154	        self._record(self.authorities, *a)
155	
156	    def add_additional(self, *a):
157	        self._record(self.additionals, *a)
158	
159	    def add_answer_raw(self, rname_, rtype, rrclass, ttl, rdata):
160	        """rtype/rrclass as raw integers (for unknown types/classes)."""
161	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", rtype, rrclass, ttl,
162	                                         len(rdata)) + rdata
163	        self.answers.append(rec)
164	
165	    def build(self):
166	        hdr = struct.pack(">HHHHHH", self.txid, self.flags, self.qdcount,
167	                          len(self.answers), len(self.authorities),
168	                          len(self.additionals))
169	        return (hdr + self._qraw + b"".join(self.answers) +
170	                b"".join(self.authorities) + b"".join(self.additionals))

173	def parse_query(data):
174	    """Return dict describing a query packet (for logging what dog sent)."""
175	    txid, flags, qd, an, ns, ar = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[:12])
176	    off = 12
177	    questions = []
178	    for _ in range(qd):
179	        labels = []
180	        while data[off] != 0:
181	            n = data[off]
182	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode("ascii", "replace"))
183	            off += 1 + n
184	        off += 1
185	        qtype, qclass = struct.unpack(">HH", data[off:off + 4])
186	        off += 4
187	        questions.append((".".join(labels), qtype, qclass))
188	    additionals = []
189	    for _ in range(ar):
190	        labels = []
191	        while data[off] != 0:
192	            if data[off] & 0xC0 == 0xC0:
193	                off += 2
194	                break
195	            n = data[off]
196	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode())
197	            off += 1 + n
198	        else:
199	            off += 1
200	        rtype, rclass, ttl, rdlen = struct.unpack(">HHIH", data[off:off + 10])
201	        off += 10
202	        additionals.append((".".join(labels), rtype, rclass, ttl,
203	                            data[off:off + rdlen].hex()))
204	        off += rdlen
205	    return {"txid": txid, "flags": flags, "qd": qd, "an": an, "ar": ar,
206	            "questions": questions, "additionals": additionals}
207

211	def serve(handler, port=5353, tcp=True, udp=True, log=True, on_query=None):
212	    """Serve DNS over UDP and TCP. handler(query_bytes) -> response bytes
213	    (or None to not respond). on_query(parsed_dict, raw) called per query."""
214	    socks = []
215	    if udp:
216	        u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
217	        u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
218	        u.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
219	        socks.append(("udp", u))
220	    if tcp:
221	        t = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
222	        t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
223	        t.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
224	        t.listen(5)
225	        socks.append(("tcp", t))
226	
227	    def loop(proto, s):
228	        while True:
229	            try:
230	                if proto == "udp":
231	                    data, addr = s.recvfrom(65535)
232	                    if on_query:
233	                        on_query(parse_query(data), data)
234	                    resp = handler(data)
235	                    if isinstance(resp, Response):
236	                        resp = resp.build()
237	                    if resp is not None:
238	                        s.sendto(resp, addr)
239	                else:
240	                    conn, _ = s.accept()
241	                    threading.Thread(target=tcp_conn,
242	                                     args=(conn, handler, on_query),
243	                                     daemon=True).start()
244	            except Exception as e:
245	                if log:
246	                    print(f"[{proto} error] {e}", flush=True)
247	
248	    def tcp_conn(conn, handler, on_query):
249	        try:
250	            while True:
251	                hdr = recv_exact(conn, 2)
252	                if not hdr:
253	                    break
254	                (length,) = struct.unpack(">H", hdr)
255	                data = recv_exact(conn, length)
256	                if on_query:
257	                    on_query(parse_query(data), data)
258	                resp = handler(data)
259	                if isinstance(resp, Response):
260	                    resp = resp.build()
261	                if resp is not None:
262	                    conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(resp)) + resp)
263	        except Exception:
264	            pass
265	        finally:
266	            conn.close()
267	
268	    for proto, s in socks:
269	        threading.Thread(target=loop, args=(proto, s), daemon=True).start()
270	    print(f"serving on 127.0.0.1:{port}", flush=True)
271	    threading.Event().wait()

274	def recv_exact(conn, n):
275	    buf = b""
276	    while len(buf) < n:
277	        chunk = conn.recv(n - len(buf))
278	        if not chunk:
279	            return None
280	        buf += chunk
281	    return buf

import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])
MODE = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "tc"

def on_query(parsed, raw, proto="?"):
    print("QUERY", parsed, flush=True)

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    if MODE == "tc":
        r.flags |= (1 << 9)  # TC bit
    r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    return r

def on_query2(parsed, raw):
    print("QUERY", parsed, flush=True)

import socket, struct, threading

def serve_tc(port):
    u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    u.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
    t = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    t.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
    t.listen(5)

    def udp_loop():
        while True:
            data, addr = u.recvfrom(65535)
            print("UDP-QUERY", parse_query(data), flush=True)
            r = handler(data)
            u.sendto(r.build(), addr)

    def tcp_conn(conn):
        try:
            hdr = conn.recv(2)
            (length,) = struct.unpack(">H", hdr)
            data = b""
            while len(data) < length:
                data += conn.recv(length - len(data))
            print("TCP-QUERY", parse_query(data), flush=True)
            r = Response(data)
            if MODE == "tcpalso_tc":
                r.flags |= (1 << 9)
            r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
            rb = r.build()
            conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(rb)) + rb)
        except Exception as e:
            print("tcp err", e, flush=True)
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def tcp_loop():
        while True:
            conn, _ = t.accept()
            threading.Thread(target=tcp_conn, args=(conn,), daemon=True).start()

    threading.Thread(target=udp_loop, daemon=True).start()
    threading.Thread(target=tcp_loop, daemon=True).start()
    print("serving", port, flush=True)
    threading.Event().wait()

serve_tc(PORT)

110	class Response:
111	    def __init__(self, query_bytes=None, txid=0x1234, qr=1, opcode=0, aa=0,
112	                 tc=0, rd=1, ra=1, z=0, ad=0, cd=0, rcode=0):
113	        self.txid = txid
114	        self.flags = ((qr << 15) | (opcode << 11) | (aa << 10) | (tc << 9) |
115	                      (rd << 8) | (ra << 7) | (z << 6) | (ad << 5) |
116	                      (cd << 4) | rcode)
117	        self.questions = []
118	        self.answers = []
119	        self.authorities = []
120	        self.additionals = []
121	        if query_bytes is not None:
122	            self.txid = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[:2])[0]
123	            qd = struct.unpack(">H", query_bytes[4:6])[0]
124	            # copy question section verbatim
125	            off = 12
126	            self._qraw = b""
127	            for _ in range(qd):
128	                start = off
129	                while query_bytes[off] != 0:
130	                    off += 1 + query_bytes[off]
131	                off += 5  # null + type + class
132	                self._qraw += query_bytes[start:off]

134	        else:
135	            self._qraw = b""
136	            self.qdcount = 0

139	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(qtype, qtype if isinstance(qtype, int) else 1)
140	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(qclass, qclass if isinstance(qclass, int) else 1)
141	        self._qraw += name(qname) + struct.pack(">HH", t, c)
142	        self.qdcount += 1

145	        t = TYPE_CODES.get(rtype, rtype if isinstance(rtype, int) else 1)
146	        c = CLASS_CODES.get(rrclass, rrclass if isinstance(rrclass, int) else 1)
147	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", t, c, ttl, len(rdata)) + rdata
148	        section.append(rec)

150	    def add_answer(self, *a):
151	        self._record(self.answers, *a)
152	
153	    def add_authority(self, *a):
154	        self._record(self.authorities, *a)
155	
156	    def add_additional(self, *a):
157	        self._record(self.additionals, *a)

159	    def add_answer_raw(self, rname_, rtype, rrclass, ttl, rdata):
160	        """rtype/rrclass as raw integers (for unknown types/classes)."""
161	        rec = name(rname_) + struct.pack(">HHIH", rtype, rrclass, ttl,
162	                                         len(rdata)) + rdata
163	        self.answers.append(rec)

165	    def build(self):
166	        hdr = struct.pack(">HHHHHH", self.txid, self.flags, self.qdcount,
167	                          len(self.answers), len(self.authorities),
168	                          len(self.additionals))
169	        return (hdr + self._qraw + b"".join(self.answers) +
170	                b"".join(self.authorities) + b"".join(self.additionals))

173	def parse_query(data):
174	    """Return dict describing a query packet (for logging what dog sent)."""
175	    txid, flags, qd, an, ns, ar = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[:12])
176	    off = 12
177	    questions = []
178	    for _ in range(qd):
179	        labels = []
180	        while data[off] != 0:
181	            n = data[off]
182	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode("ascii", "replace"))
183	            off += 1 + n
184	        off += 1
185	        qtype, qclass = struct.unpack(">HH", data[off:off + 4])
186	        off += 4
187	        questions.append((".".join(labels), qtype, qclass))
188	    additionals = []
189	    for _ in range(ar):
190	        labels = []
191	        while data[off] != 0:
192	            if data[off] & 0xC0 == 0xC0:
193	                off += 2
194	                break
195	            n = data[off]
196	            labels.append(data[off + 1:off + 1 + n].decode())
197	            off += 1 + n
198	        else:
199	            off += 1
200	        rtype, rclass, ttl, rdlen = struct.unpack(">HHIH", data[off:off + 10])
201	        off += 10
202	        additionals.append((".".join(labels), rtype, rclass, ttl,
203	                            data[off:off + rdlen].hex()))
204	        off += rdlen
205	    return {"txid": txid, "flags": flags, "qd": qd, "an": an, "ar": ar,
206	            "questions": questions, "additionals": additionals}

211	def serve(handler, port=5353, tcp=True, udp=True, log=True, on_query=None):
212	    """Serve DNS over UDP and TCP. handler(query_bytes) -> response bytes
213	    (or None to not respond). on_query(parsed_dict, raw) called per query."""
214	    socks = []
215	    if udp:
216	        u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
217	        u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
218	        u.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
219	        socks.append(("udp", u))
220	    if tcp:
221	        t = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
222	        t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
223	        t.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
224	        t.listen(5)
225	        socks.append(("tcp", t))
226	
227	    def loop(proto, s):
228	        while True:
229	            try:
230	                if proto == "udp":
231	                    data, addr = s.recvfrom(65535)
232	                    if on_query:
233	                        on_query(parse_query(data), data)
234	                    resp = handler(data)
235	                    if isinstance(resp, Response):
236	                        resp = resp.build()
237	                    if resp is not None:
238	                        s.sendto(resp, addr)
239	                else:
240	                    conn, _ = s.accept()
241	                    threading.Thread(target=tcp_conn,
242	                                     args=(conn, handler, on_query),
243	                                     daemon=True).start()
244	            except Exception as e:
245	                if log:
246	                    print(f"[{proto} error] {e}", flush=True)
247	
248	    def tcp_conn(conn, handler, on_query):
249	        try:
250	            while True:
251	                hdr = recv_exact(conn, 2)
252	                if not hdr:
253	                    break
254	                (length,) = struct.unpack(">H", hdr)
255	                data = recv_exact(conn, length)
256	                if on_query:
257	                    on_query(parse_query(data), data)
258	                resp = handler(data)
259	                if isinstance(resp, Response):
260	                    resp = resp.build()
261	                if resp is not None:
262	                    conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(resp)) + resp)
263	        except Exception:
264	            pass
265	        finally:
266	            conn.close()
267	
268	    for proto, s in socks:
269	        threading.Thread(target=loop, args=(proto, s), daemon=True).start()
270	    print(f"serving on 127.0.0.1:{port}", flush=True)
271	    threading.Event().wait()
272	
273	
274	def recv_exact(conn, n):
275	    buf = b""
276	    while len(buf) < n:
277	        chunk = conn.recv(n - len(buf))
278	        if not chunk:
279	            return None
280	        buf += chunk
281	    return buf

"""Scenario server for text-output probing. Usage: textout_srv.py PORT SCENARIO"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])
SCEN = sys.argv[2]

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    if SCEN == "align_mixed":
        # mixed type widths, name widths, ttl widths
        r.add_answer("a.b", "A", 0, A("1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "AAAA", 4294967295, AAAA("::1"))
        r.add_answer("medium.name.example", "TXT", 3600, TXT("x"))
        r.add_answer_raw("veryveryverylongname.example.org", 99, 1, 59, b"\x01\x02\x03\x04")
    elif SCEN == "align_narrow":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    elif SCEN == "sections":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "AAAA", 300, AAAA("::1"))
        r.add_authority("example.com", "NS", 3600, name("ns1.example.com"))
        r.add_authority("example.com", "SOA", 3600, SOA("ns1.example.com", "hostmaster.example.com", 1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
        r.add_additional("ns1.example.com", "A", 60, A("5.6.7.8"))
        r.add_additional("ns1.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT("hello"))
    elif SCEN == "sections_opt":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_authority("example.com", "NS", 3600, name("ns1.example.com"))
        r.add_additional("ns1.example.com", "A", 60, A("5.6.7.8"))
        r.add_additional("", "OPT", 0, OPT(4096, 0, 0, 0x8000))
    elif SCEN == "sections_opt_only":
        # OPT as the only additional
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_additional("", "OPT", 0, OPT(4096, 0, 0, 0))
    elif SCEN == "empty_ans_auth":
        # NOERROR, empty answers, authority SOA (NODATA)
        r.add_authority("example.com", "SOA", 3600, SOA("ns1.example.com", "hostmaster.example.com", 1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
    elif SCEN == "multi_a":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.1.1.1"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("2.2.2.2"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("3.3.3.3"))
    elif SCEN == "cname_chain":
        r.add_answer("www.example.com", "CNAME", 300, name("example.com"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    elif SCEN.startswith("rcode_"):
        rcode = int(SCEN.split("_")[1])
        r.flags = (r.flags & ~0xF) | rcode
        if rcode == 0:
            pass  # NOERROR empty
    elif SCEN.startswith("flags_"):
        # flags_AA_TC_RD_RA_AD_CD  e.g. flags_1_0_1_1_0_0
        parts = SCEN.split("_")[1:]
        aa, tc, rd, ra, ad, cd = map(int, parts)
        r.flags = (1 << 15) | (aa << 10) | (tc << 9) | (rd << 8) | (ra << 7) | (ad << 5) | (cd << 4)
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    elif SCEN == "tc_only":
        # truncated UDP response (no records)
        r.flags |= 0x0200
    return r

def on_query(parsed, raw):
    print(parsed, flush=True)

serve(handler, port=PORT, on_query=on_query, log=False)

        r.flags = (r.flags & ~0xF) | rcode
        if rcode == 0:
            pass  # NOERROR empty
    elif SCEN.startswith("flags_"):
        # flags_AA_TC_RD_RA_AD_CD  e.g. flags_1_0_1_1_0_0
        parts = SCEN.split("_")[1:]
        aa, tc, rd, ra, ad, cd = map(int, parts)
        r.flags = (1 << 15) | (aa << 10) | (tc << 9) | (rd << 8) | (ra << 7) | (ad << 5) | (cd << 4)
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    elif SCEN == "tc_only":
        # truncated UDP response (no records)
        r.flags |= 0x0200
    return r

def on_query(parsed, raw):
    print(parsed, flush=True)

serve(handler, port=PORT, on_query=on_query, log=False)
