NAME
====

dog — a command-line DNS client


SYNOPSIS
========

`dog [options] [domains...]`

**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.


EXAMPLES
========

`dog example.net`
: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings

`dog example.net MX`
: ...looking up `MX` records instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
: ...using a specific nameserver instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
: ...using TCP rather than UDP

`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
: As above, but using explicit arguments


QUERY OPTIONS
=============

`-q`, `--query=HOST`
: Host name or domain name to query.

`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Flexible server for misc probing. Usage: misc2_server.py PORT MODE

Modes:
  a        - simple A answer for whatever was queried
  classes  - answers with IN, CH, HS and unknown-class (99, 255) records
  echo     - echo back queried name verbatim in a TXT answer
  nxdomain - rcode 3
"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

mode = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "a"


def qname_of(q):
    p = parse_query(q)
    return p["questions"][0][0] if p["questions"] else "example.com"


def handler(q):
    qn = qname_of(q)
    if mode == "a":
        r = Response(q)
        r.add_answer(qn, "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
        return r
    if mode == "classes":
        r = Response(q, aa=1)
        r.add_answer(qn, "TXT", 60, TXT("class-IN"), rrclass="IN")
        r.add_answer(qn, "TXT", 60, TXT("class-CH"), rrclass="CH")
        r.add_answer(qn, "TXT", 60, TXT("class-HS"), rrclass="HS")
        r.add_answer_raw(qn, 16, 99, 60, TXT("class-99"))
        r.add_answer_raw(qn, 16, 255, 60, TXT("class-255"))
        r.add_answer_raw(qn, 1, 3, 60, A("9.9.9.9"))   # A record, class CH
        r.add_answer_raw(qn, 1, 4, 60, A("8.8.8.8"))   # A record, class HS
        return r
    if mode == "echo":
        r = Response(q)
        r.add_answer(qn, "TXT", 60, TXT("echo"))
        return r
    if mode == "nxdomain":
        return Response(q, rcode=3, aa=1)
    if mode == "ptr":
        r = Response(q)
        r.add_answer(qn, "PTR", 300, name("host.example.com"))
        return r
    if mode == "none":
        return None  # never respond (timeout test)


def on_query(parsed, raw):
    print("QUERY:", parsed, flush=True)
    print("RAW:", raw.hex(), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(handler, port=int(sys.argv[1]), on_query=on_query)

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

PORT = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 5541

MODE = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "soa"

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    if MODE == "soa":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "SOA", 300, SOA("ns1.example.com", "hostmaster.example.com", 2020010101, 7200, 3600, 1209600, 300))
    elif MODE == "naptr":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "NAPTR", 300, NAPTR(100, 50, "s", "SIP+D2U", "!^.*$!sip:info@example.com!", "_sip._udp.example.com"))
    elif MODE == "caa":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "CAA", 300, CAA(128, "issue", "letsencrypt.org"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "CAA", 300, CAA(1, "tbs", "x"))
    elif MODE == "opt":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_additional(".", "OPT", 0, OPT(4096, 0, 0, 0x8000, b"\x00\x0a\x00\x04\xde\xad\xbe\xef"))
    elif MODE == "classes":
        # unknown class 99 on A record; CH class; HS class
        r.add_answer_raw("example.com", 1, 99, 60, A("1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_answer_raw("example.com", 1, 3, 60, A("5.6.7.8"))
        r.add_answer_raw("example.com", 1, 4, 60, A("9.10.11.12"))
    elif MODE == "bigttl":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 4294967295, A("1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 0, A("5.6.7.8"))
    elif MODE == "txt":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "TXT", 300, TXT('quote " backslash \\ tab\t newline\n'))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "TXT", 300, TXT('café ☃ 日本語'))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "TXT", 300, TXT(b'\xff\xfe\x80bad utf8'))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "TXT", 300, TXT(''))
    elif MODE == "empty":
        pass  # NOERROR, no records
    elif MODE == "mx0":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "MX", 300, MX(0, "."))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "MX", 300, MX(65535, "mail.example.com"))
    return r

serve(handler, port=PORT, log=True)

    return r

serve(handler, port=PORT, log=True)

"""Per-query server: response depends on queried name/type."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *
import struct

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    off = 12
    labels = []
    while q[off] != 0:
        n = q[off]
        labels.append(q[off+1:off+1+n].decode())
        off += 1 + n
    off += 1
    qtype, qclass = struct.unpack(">HH", q[off:off+4])
    qname = ".".join(labels)
    if qname == "wide.example.org":
        # wide response
        r.add_answer(qname, "AAAA", 4294967295, AAAA("::1"))
        r.add_answer(qname, "A", 0, A("1.2.3.4"))
    else:
        r.add_answer(qname, "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    return r

serve(handler, port=PORT, log=False)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Server bound to a custom loopback IP and port (for default-resolver tests).
Usage: misc_bind_server.py IP PORT MODE"""
import sys, socket, struct, threading
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import Response, A, parse_query

ip, port = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
mode = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "a"


def handler(q):
    p = parse_query(q)
    qn = p["questions"][0][0] if p["questions"] else "example.com"
    if mode == "a":
        r = Response(q)
        r.add_answer(qn, "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
        return r
    return Response(q)


u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
u.bind((ip, port))
t = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
t.bind((ip, port))
t.listen(5)


def udp_loop():
    while True:
        data, addr = u.recvfrom(65535)
        print("UDP QUERY from", addr, parse_query(data), flush=True)
        print("RAW:", data.hex(), flush=True)
        r = handler(data)
        u.sendto(r.build(), addr)


def tcp_loop():
    while True:
        conn, addr = t.accept()
        print("TCP CONN from", addr, flush=True)
        conn.close()


threading.Thread(target=udp_loop, daemon=True).start()
threading.Thread(target=tcp_loop, daemon=True).start()
print(f"serving on {ip}:{port}", flush=True)
threading.Event().wait()

"""Delay responses for specific names to test output ordering."""
import sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *
import struct

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])

def qname_of(q):
    off = 12
    labels = []
    while q[off] != 0:
        n = q[off]
        labels.append(q[off+1:off+1+n].decode())
        off += 1 + n
    return ".".join(labels)

def handler(q):
    qn = qname_of(q)
    if qn.startswith("slow"):
        time.sleep(1.5)
    r = Response(q)
    if qn.startswith("nx"):
        r.flags |= 3
        return r
    r.add_answer(qn, "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
    return r

serve(handler, port=PORT, log=False)

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *
import struct

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])
MODE = sys.argv[2]

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    if MODE == "optv":
        # version=1, ext_rcode=2, flags=0x8000, payload 1232, two options
        opts = b"\x00\x0a\x00\x02\x01\x02" + b"\x00\x03\x00\x00"
        r.add_additional(".", "OPT", 0, OPT(1232, 2, 1, 0x8000, opts))
    elif MODE == "loc":
        # various LOC values
        r.add_answer("a.example.com", "LOC", 300, LOC(0, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80000000, 0x80000000, 10000000))
        r.add_answer("b.example.com", "LOC", 300, LOC(0, 0x99, 0x99, 0x99, 0x80000000 - 1, 0x80000000 + 1, 10000000 - 100500))
        r.add_answer("c.example.com", "LOC", 300, LOC(0, 0x13, 0x12, 0x11, 0x80000000 + 52968400, 0x80000000 - 134150200, 10000000 + 100))
    elif MODE == "names":
        # weird names: space, dot-in-label, backslash, quote, non-ascii, wildcard
        r.add_answer("we ird.example.com", "A", 300, A("1.1.1.1"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "CNAME", 300, name("tar\\get.example.com"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "NS", 300, name('qu"ote.example.com'))
        r.add_answer("*.example.com", "TXT", 300, TXT("wild"))
        r.add_answer("café.example.com", "A", 300, A("2.2.2.2"))
    elif MODE == "aaaa":
        r.add_answer("example.com", "AAAA", 300, AAAA("::1"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "AAAA", 300, AAAA("::ffff:1.2.3.4"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "AAAA", 300, AAAA("2001:db8::1"))
        r.add_answer("example.com", "AAAA", 300, AAAA("fe80::a00:27ff:fe4e:66a1"))
    elif MODE == "badlen":
        # A record with wrong rdlength (3 bytes)
        r.add_answer_raw("example.com", 1, 1, 60, b"\x01\x02\x03")
    return r

serve(handler, port=PORT, log=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""TTL/duration formatting edge cases."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import

TTLS = [0, 1, 2, 59, 60, 61, 119, 120, 3599, 3600, 3601, 3661,
        86399, 86400, 86401, 90061, 604799, 604800, 604801,
        2592000, 2678400, 31536000, 2147483647, 2147483648, 4294967295]

def handler(q):

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])

def bname(*labels):
    out = b""
    for l in labels:
        b = l.encode() if isinstance(l, str) else l
        out += bytes([len(b)]) + b
    return out + b"\x00"

def handler(q):

    r.answers.append(bname("we ird", "example", "com") + __import__("struct").pack(">HHIH", 1, 1, 300, 4) + A("1.1.1.1"))

    r.answers.append(bname("café".encode(), "example", "com") + __import__("struct").pack(">HHIH", 1, 1, 300, 4) + A("2.2.2.2"))
    r.add_answer("example.com", "PTR", 300, bname("dot.in.label", "example", "com"))
    return r

serve(handler, port=PORT, log=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""TXT/HINFO string edge cases."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    r.add_answer("empty.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT(b""))
    r.add_answer("multi.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT(b"a", b"", b"c"))
    r.add_answer("quote.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT(b'say "hi" to \\me\\'))
    r.add_answer("utf8.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT("héllo wörld ☃".encode()))
    r.add_answer("ctrl.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT(b"a\x00b\x01\x1f\x7f\xff\t\n"))
    r.add_answer("long.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT(b"x" * 255))
    r.add_answer("sp.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT(b"v=spf1 include:_spf.example.com ~all"))
    r.add_answer("hi2.example.com", "HINFO", 60, HINFO(b'cpu "x"', b""))
    r.add_answer("semicol.example.com", "TXT", 60, TXT(b"a;b(c)"))
    return r

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(handler, port=int(sys.argv[1]))

"""Respond to UDP with a fixed byte pattern given on argv."""
import sys, socket
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import parse_query

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])
PATTERN = sys.argv[2]

u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
u.bind(("127.0.0.1", PORT))
print("serving", PORT, PATTERN, flush=True)
while True:
    data, addr = u.recvfrom(65535)
    print("QUERY", parse_query(data), flush=True)
    if PATTERN == "zeros40":
        resp = b"\x00" * 40
    elif PATTERN == "zeros12":
        resp = b"\x00" * 12
    elif PATTERN == "empty":
        resp = b""
    elif PATTERN == "hdr_only":
        # valid header copied from query with qr=1, but qd=1 and no question bytes
        resp = bytearray(data[:12]); resp[2] |= 0x80; resp = bytes(resp)
    elif PATTERN == "copy_nohdr":
        resp = data[12:]
    elif PATTERN == "ff40":
        resp = b"\xff" * 40
    else:
        resp = bytes.fromhex(PATTERN)
    u.sendto(resp, addr)

"""TCP-only server that logs raw bytes (incl. length prefix) and responds per mode."""
import sys, socket, struct, threading, os
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])
MODE = sys.argv[2]

t = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
t.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
t.bind(("127.0.0.1", PORT))
t.listen(5)
print("serving", PORT, MODE, flush=True)

def conn_loop(conn):
    try:
        while True:
            hdr = b""
            while len(hdr) < 2:
                c = conn.recv(2 - len(hdr))
                if not c:
                    print("CLIENT-CLOSED (before/during length prefix)", flush=True)
                    return
                hdr += c
            (length,) = struct.unpack(">H", hdr)
            data = b""
            while len(data) < length:
                c = conn.recv(length - len(data))
                if not c:
                    print("CLIENT-CLOSED mid-query", flush=True)
                    return
                data += c
            print("RAW-QUERY-FRAME len=%d hex=%s" % (length, (hdr + data).hex()), flush=True)
            print("PARSED", parse_query(data), flush=True)
            if MODE == "normal":
                r = Response(data)
                r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
                rb = r.build()
                conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(rb)) + rb)
                print("SENT len=%d hex=%s" % (len(rb), rb.hex()), flush=True)
            elif MODE == "garbage":
                g = os.urandom(30)
                conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(g)) + g)
            elif MODE == "garbage_noframe":
                conn.sendall(os.urandom(30))
            elif MODE == "badlen_big":
                # announce 500 bytes, send 10, keep open briefly then close
                conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", 500) + b"\x00" * 10)
                conn.close(); return
            elif MODE == "badlen_small":
                # valid response but length prefix 4 less than actual
                r = Response(data)
                r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
                rb = r.build()
                conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(rb) - 4) + rb)
                return
            elif MODE == "close_now":
                return
            elif MODE == "close_after_read":
                return
            elif MODE == "silent":
                threading.Event().wait()
            elif MODE == "wrong_txid":
                r = Response(data)
                r.txid = (r.txid + 1) & 0xFFFF
                r.add_answer("example.com", "A", 300, A("1.2.3.4"))
                rb = r.build()
                conn.sendall(struct.pack(">H", len(rb)) + rb)
    except Exception as e:
        print("conn err", repr(e), flush=True)
    finally:
        try: conn.close()
        except Exception: pass

while True:
    conn, _ = t.accept()
    threading.Thread(target=conn_loop, args=(conn,), daemon=True).start()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Serve a single TXT-ish record chosen by index."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

RECS = [
    ("empty.example.com", "TXT", TXT(b"")),
    ("multi.example.com", "TXT", TXT(b"a", b"", b"c")),
    ("quote.example.com", "TXT", TXT(b'say "hi" to \\me\\')),
    ("utf8.example.com", "TXT", TXT("héllo wörld ☃".encode())),
    ("ctrl.example.com", "TXT", TXT(b"a\x00b\x01\x1f\x7f\xff\t\n")),
    ("long.example.com", "TXT", TXT(b"x" * 254)),
    ("sp.example.com", "TXT", TXT(b"v=spf1 include:_spf.example.com ~all")),
    ("hi2.example.com", "HINFO", HINFO(b'cpu "x"', b"")),
    ("semicol.example.com", "TXT", TXT(b"a;b(c)")),
]

IDX = int(sys.argv[2])

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    n, t, d = RECS[IDX]
    r.add_answer(n, t, 60, d)
    return r

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(handler, port=int(sys.argv[1]))

# Spec: command-line argument parsing (`dog`)

Probed binary: `/workspace/executable` (`dog v0.1.0`-ish; version string says
`v0.2.0-pre [d3a34280] built on 2026-04-17 (pre-release!)`).
All probes run against a fake DNS server on `127.0.0.1:5510` that logs every
query and replies with a fixed `A example.com. 300 1.2.3.4` answer. "Wire"
notes below describe the query bytes dog sent. Unless stated otherwise every
command was run as `timeout 10 ./executable ...` with stdout piped (not a TTY).

Exit-code summary: `0` ok · `1` network/I/O/TLS error · `2` short mode, no
result · `3` argument problem · `4` resolver-config problem (not triggered
during these probes). Additionally `-H` with a non-URL nameserver **panics**
(exit 134 / SIGABRT).

---

## 1. Meta options

### `--help` / `-?`
- Both print the identical 1856-byte help text to **stdout**, exit `0`.
- Running `dog` with **no arguments at all**, or with arguments that contain
  **no domain** (e.g. `dog -1`, `dog -U`, `dog A @127.0.0.1:5510`,
  `dog @127.0.0.1:5510`), prints the *same* help text to **stdout** but exits
  **`3`**. Nothing on stderr in that case.
- `--help example.com` → help on stdout, exit `0` (short-circuits, no query).
- `--help --frobnicate` → parse error wins: exit 3, stderr
  `dog: Invalid options: Unrecognized option: 'frobnicate'`.
- `--help=foo` → exit 3, `dog: Invalid options: Option 'help' does not take an argument`.
- Exact help bytes (no ANSI codes; the `●` is U+25CF, UTF-8 `E2 97 8F`;
  every line ends `\n`, including the last):

```
dog ● command-line DNS client

Usage:
  dog [OPTIONS] [--] <arguments>

Examples:
  dog example.net                          Query a domain using default settings
  dog example.net MX                       ...looking up MX records instead
  dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1              ...using a specific nameserver instead
  dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T           ...using TCP rather than UDP
  dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T   As above, but using explicit arguments

Query options:
  <arguments>              Human-readable host names, nameservers, types, or classes
  -q, --query=HOST         Host name or domain name to query
  -t, --type=TYPE          Type of the DNS record being queried (A, MX, NS...)
  -n, --nameserver=ADDR    Address of the nameserver to send packets to
  --class=CLASS            Network class of the DNS record being queried (IN, CH, HS)

Sending options:
  --edns=SETTING           Whether to OPT in to EDNS (disable, hide, show)
  --txid=NUMBER            Set the transaction ID to a specific value
  -Z=TWEAKS                Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks

Protocol options:
  -U, --udp                Use the DNS protocol over UDP
  -T, --tcp                Use the DNS protocol over TCP
  -S, --tls                Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol
  -H, --https              Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol

Output options:
  -1, --short              Short mode: display nothing but the first result
  -J, --json               Display the output as JSON
  --color, --colour=WHEN   When to colourise the output (always, automatic, never)
  --seconds                Do not format durations, display them as seconds
  --time                   Print how long the response took to arrive

Meta options:
  -?, --help               Print list of command-line options
  -v, --version            Print version information
```

### `--version` / `-v`
- Both print the identical **114-byte** text to stdout, exit `0`.
- Exact bytes (od -c verified). Quirk: there is a **literal `m`** before the
  URL (looks like a leftover of a broken escape sequence — reproduce it):

```
dog ● command-line DNS client\n
v0.2.0-pre [d3a34280] built on 2026-04-17 (pre-release!)\n
mhttps://dns.lookup.dog/\n
```

- `--version example.com` / `-v -T` → version printed, exit 0 (short-circuits).
- `--version --frobnicate` → exit 3, unrecognized-option error (parse errors
  take precedence over both `--version` and `--help`, regardless of order).
- `-h` and `-V` are NOT aliases: `dog: Invalid options: Unrecognized option: 'h'` (exit 3).

---

## 2. Option syntax rules (getopts-style)

- Long options accept `--opt=value` **and** `--opt value` (next argument is
  consumed as the value, even if it looks like data: `--edns example.com`
  consumes `example.com` as the EDNS value → `Invalid EDNS setting "example.com"`).
- `--color` also consumes the next token even if it looks like a flag:
  `--color -1 example.com ...` → `-1` is the color value (invalid → ignored),
  so short mode is NOT active.
- Short options accept attached values: `-tMX`, `-qexample.com`, `-Zaa`,
  `-Zbufsize=512` all work. `-t=MX` → value is literally `=MX`
  → `Invalid query type "=MX"`. `-Z=aa` → `Invalid protocol tweak "=aa"`.
- Short flags cluster: `-1J`, `-J1`, `-UT`, `-U1J` all work. In a cluster a
  value-taking option consumes the rest of the cluster: `-1tMX` = `-1 -t MX`;
  `-1t MX` = `-1 -t MX` too.
- No long-option abbreviation: `--typ MX` → `Unrecognized option: 'typ'`.
- Unknown options: `--frobnicate` → `Unrecognized option: 'frobnicate'`;
  `-x` → `Unrecognized option: 'x'`; `-1x` → `Unrecognized option: 'x'`;
  `--foo=bar` → `Unrecognized option: 'foo'` (value not shown);
  `--foo-bar` → `Unrecognized option: 'foo-bar'`.
- A flag given a value: `--udp=true` → `Option 'udp' does not take an argument`;
  `--help=foo` → `Option 'help' does not take an argument`.
- Missing value (option last on the line): `dog: Invalid options: Argument to option 'X' missing`
  where X is the option as spelled: `t`, `type`, `q`, `query`, `n`, `nameserver`,
  `class`, `edns`, `txid`, `Z`, `colour`. (Verified for `--type`, `-t`,
  `--edns`, `--class`, `--txid`, `-Z`, `--query`, `-n`, `--colour`.)
- A value-taking option followed by another flag consumes that flag as its
  value: `-t -T example.com` → `Invalid query type "-T"`.
- All argument errors go to **stderr**, exact prefix `dog: Invalid options: `,
  one line, trailing `\n`, exit **`3`**, nothing on stdout (except the
  no-domain case which prints help to stdout).

### `--` separator
- Everything after `--` is a plain argument, but **guessing still applies**:
  `example.com -- MX @ns` and `-- example.com MX @ns` still treat `MX` as a
  type and `@ns` as a nameserver (wire: qtype 15).
- A plain argument starting with `-` is rejected:
  `dog -- -T` → `Invalid domain "-T"`; `-1 -- -J example.com` →
  `Invalid domain "-J"`; `dog - example.com` → `Invalid domain "-"`.
  (Exit 3 in all cases.)

### Duplicates
- Repeatable (accumulate): `-q/--query`, `-t/--type`, `-n/--nameserver`,
  `--class`, `-Z`. Repeated values produce multiple queries (see §5).
  `-Z aa -Z aa` is fine.
- Not repeatable — second occurrence → exit 3,
  `dog: Invalid options: Option 'X' given more than once` where X is the long
  name. Verified: `txid`, `edns`, `udp` (`-U -U` or `-U --udp`), `time`,
  `seconds`, `short` (`-1 -1`), `json` (`-J -J`).
- `--color` + `--colour` together do NOT error (see §6).

---

## 3. Value validation (all exit 3 on failure, message format given)

### `-t, --type=TYPE`
Accepted, case-insensitively (`mx`, `Mx`, `iXfR` work), the following 41
names — same set as the plain-argument guesser:

| name | num | name | num | name | num |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 | NS | 2 | CNAME | 5 |
| SOA | 6 | PTR | 12 | HINFO | 13 |
| MX | 15 | TXT | 16 | RP | 17 |
| AFSDB | 18 | KEY | 25 | AAAA | 28 |
| LOC | 29 | SRV | 33 | NAPTR | 35 |
| KX | 36 | DNAME | 39 | APL | 42 |
| DS | 43 | RRSIG | 46 | NSEC | 47 |
| DHCID | 49 | NSEC3 | 50 | NSEC3PARAM | 51 |
| TLSA | 52 | CDNSKEY | 60 | CDS | 59 |
| OPENPGPKEY | 61 | EUI48 | 108 | EUI64 | 109 |
| TKEY | 249 | TSIG | 250 | IXFR | 251 |
| AXFR | 252 | ANY | 255 | URI | 256 |
| CAA | 257 | TA | 32768 | DLV | 32769 |

(SSHFP=44 is also accepted — verified via plain arg; full accepted set:
A AAAA AFSDB ANY APL AXFR CAA CDNSKEY CDS CNAME DHCID DLV DNAME DS EUI48
EUI64 HINFO IXFR KEY KX LOC MX NAPTR NS NSEC NSEC3 NSEC3PARAM OPENPGPKEY PTR
RP RRSIG SOA SRV SSHFP TA TKEY TLSA TSIG TXT URI.)

- Also accepted: decimal numbers `0`–`65535` (`-t 0`, `-t 1`, `-t 255`,
  `-t 65535` all sent on the wire; `+1` and `01` accepted).
- Rejected (`dog: Invalid options: Invalid query type "X"`, exit 3):
  any unknown name (`FOO`, `DNSKEY`, `SVCB`, `HTTPS`, `SPF`, `ZONEMD`,
  `WKS`, `MD`, `MF`, `MB`, `MG`, `MR`, `MINFO`, `NULL`, `MAILA`, `MAILB`,
  `ALL`, `NONE` — note DNSKEY/SVCB/HTTPS are **not** known!), `65536`, `-1`,
  `0x10`, `*` (and shell glob `*`), empty string (`Invalid query type ""`).
- `OPT` is special: `Invalid query type "OPT"`? No — as an explicit `-t OPT`
  or plain arg it yields: `dog: Invalid options: OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)`.
- Validation happens before any network: `-t FOO example.com` → exit 3, no query.

### `--class=CLASS`
- Accepted case-insensitively: `IN`=1, `CH`=3, `HS`=4 (`--class=ch` works).
- Accepted numerically: `0`–`65535` (`--class=0`, `--class=1`,
  `--class=65535`, `+1`, `01` OK).
- Rejected: `ANY`, `NONE`, `none`, `XX`, `65536`, `-1`, empty →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "X"`.

### `--txid=NUMBER`
- Accepted: `0`–`65535` decimal, plus `+5` (→5), leading zeros (`0007`→7),
  and **hex with lowercase `0x` prefix** (`0x10`→16). Verified on the wire
  (`0005…`, `0010…`, `ffff…` as first two bytes).
- Rejected: `65536`, `-1`, `abc`, `0X10` (capital X!), ` 5`, `5 ` (no
  trimming), empty, huge numbers →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "X"`.
- Given more than once → `Option 'txid' given more than once`.
- One `--txid` applies to ALL queries when multiple are sent (both queries
  used txid 42).

### `--edns=SETTING`
- Accepted (case-SENSITIVE, lowercase only): `disable`, `hide`, `show`.
- `disable` → no OPT record in the query (ARCOUNT=0).
- `hide` and `show` → byte-identical queries (OPT record, UDP payload 512);
  they differ only in output rendering.
- Rejected: `bogus`, `DISABLE`, `` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid EDNS setting "X"`.

### `-Z=TWEAKS` (repeatable; each `-Z` takes exactly ONE tweak)
- `aa` → sets AA bit (flags 0x0500 with RD). `ad` → 0x0120. `cd` → 0x0110.
  Combined `-Z aa -Z ad -Z cd` → flags 0x0530.
- `bufsize=NUM` → sets OPT UDP payload size (`bufsize=1024` → 0x0400,
  `bufsize=4096` → 0x1000, `bufsize=0` → 0x0000). Range 0–65535;
  `bufsize=99999`, `bufsize=-1`, `bufsize=abc` →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "bufsize=99999"` etc.
- Case-sensitive: `-Z AA` → `Invalid protocol tweak "AA"`.
- No comma syntax: `-Z aa,ad` → `Invalid protocol tweak "aa,ad"`.
- Any other value (e.g. `bogus`, `example.com`, `=aa`, empty) →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "X"`.

### `--color, --colour=WHEN`
- Accepted values: `always`, `automatic`, `never` (case-sensitive in effect;
  see below). Both spellings are the same option family, but...
- **Surprise 1:** invalid values are silently accepted — no error, exit
  unaffected. `--color=bogus`, `--color=ALWAYS` behave like `automatic`
  (no color when stdout is not a TTY).
- **Surprise 2:** when both spellings are given, `--color` wins over
  `--colour` **regardless of order**: `--color=never --colour=always` → no
  color; `--colour=always --color=never` → no color; `--color=always
  --colour=never` → color. (i.e. `--colour` is only a fallback used when
  `--color` is absent.)
- `--color always` (space form) works and colorizes.
- `always` with piped stdout produced: `^[[1;32mA^[[0m ^[[1;34mexample.com.^[[0m 5m00s   1.2.3.4`
  (type bold green `1;32`, name bold blue `1;34`, reset `0`).

### Conflicting / combined output & protocol options
- `-1` + `-J` (either order, incl. clusters `-1J`/`-J1`): **short mode wins**;
  output is just `1.2.3.4\n`, exit 0. No error.
- `-U -T` / `-T -U` / `-UT`: **no error — protocols accumulate**, one query
  per transport, in the order the flags were given. Against a TCP-only server:
  `-U -T` printed `Error [network]: Connection refused (os error 111)` (stderr)
  then the answer (stdout), exit **1**; `-T -U` printed the answer then the
  error, exit **1**. Against a dual-stack server both succeed and the answer
  table is printed twice, exit 0.
- `-S` (TLS) to a plain-TCP server **hangs** (no data ever arrives; killed by
  `timeout`, exit 124). `-T -S` likewise hangs on the TLS leg.
- `-H` with a non-URL nameserver (e.g. `example.com -H @127.0.0.1:5510`):
  **panics**. stderr exactly (PID varies; the final line about core dump comes
  from `timeout`, not dog):
  ```
  \nthread 'main' (7937) panicked at dns-transport/src/https.rs:42:50:\nInvalid HTTPS nameserver\nnote: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n
  ```
  Exit **134** (SIGABRT, core dumped).
- `-H -n https://127.0.0.1:5512/dns-query example.com` → no panic, but exit 1
  with `Error [network]: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`
  (observed in this offline env).

---

## 4. Plain-argument guessing rules

Every non-option argument (including those after `--`) is classified by the
first matching rule:

1. **Starts with `@`** → nameserver. The remainder is parsed as
   `host`, `host:port`, `[v6addr]`, `[v6addr]:port`. Details:
   - `@127.0.0.1:5510` works (port parsed numerically).
   - `@1.2.3.4:5510` → tries that IP (exit 1 `Network is unreachable (os error 101)` offline).
   - `@[::1]:5510` → parsed as IPv6; exit 1 `Address family not supported by protocol (os error 97)` here.
   - `@::1` (bare v6, no brackets) → NOT parsed as IPv6; treated as a hostname
     for the OS resolver → `Error [network]: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`, exit 1.
   - `@localhost:5510` → works (OS resolves `localhost`; dog does not resolve it itself).
   - `@` alone, `@-foo` → hostname lookup fails: same `failed to lookup address information` error, exit 1.
   - `@127.0.0.1:` or `@127.0.0.1:abc` → `Error [network]: invalid port value`, exit 1.
   - `@127.0.0.1:0` → connects to port 0 → `Connection refused (os error 111)`.
   - `@https://127.0.0.1:5512/dns-query` → `Error [network]: invalid port value`, exit 1 (plain @URL does not switch to HTTPS).
   - These are runtime/network errors (exit 1), not argument errors (exit 3).
2. **Case-insensitive match of a known TYPE name** (the 41-name list in §3,
   e.g. `A`, `a`, `MX`, `any`, `iXfR`) → query type. `OPT` → the special
   `OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)` error.
3. **Case-insensitive match of `IN`, `CH`, `HS`** → query class.
4. **Anything else** → domain name. This includes: unknown uppercase words
   (`FOO` → qname `foo`), unknown type-like strings (`DNSKEY`, `SVCB`,
   `HTTPS`, `ALL`, `NONE`, `NULL`, `WKS`...), pure numbers (`123`, `255`,
   `15` → qnames `123`, `255`, `15`), IPv4-looking strings (`1.2.3.4` →
   qname `1.2.3.4`), bare IPv6 (`::1` → qname literally `::1`, one label),
   names with hyphens/underscores (`my-host.example.com`,
   `_dmarc.example.com`), weird TLDs (`example.xyzzy`), trailing dots
   (`example.com.` → sent as `example.com`), `mx.`/`in.` (trailing dot
   defeats type/class matching → domains `mx`, `in`), empty string `` and
   `.` (both → root qname, zero labels).
5. Plain args starting with `-` → `Invalid domain "X"`, exit 3.

Domain normalization (applies to plain domains AND `-q` values):
- **Lowercased**: `ExAmPle.CoM` and `-q ExAmPle.COM` → wire qname `example.com`.
- **IDNA/punycode-encoded**: `bücher.de` → `xn--bcher-kva.de` on the wire.

Explicit options bypass guessing:
- `-q @foo` → qname literally `@foo` (one label), not a nameserver.
- `-n @127.0.0.1:5510` → the `@` is NOT stripped; `@127.0.0.1` goes to the OS
  resolver → `failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`, exit 1.
- `-q ''` → root query (zero-label qname).

A run needs ≥1 domain: if the args contain only types/classes/nameservers
(`dog A @127.0.0.1:5510`, `dog IN @ns`, `dog @ns`), help is printed to stdout,
exit 3.

---

## 5. Multiple values → cross-product queries

- Repeating `-q`, `-t`, `-n`, `--class` (or mixing plain and explicit values)
  accumulates lists; dog sends one query per combination. Verified:
  - `-q a.com -q b.com @ns` → 2 queries (a.com, b.com).
  - `-t A -t MX example.com` → 2 queries (A then MX).
  - `--class=IN --class=CH` → qclass 1 then 3. `example.com CH HS` → same.
  - `-n ns -n ns example.com` (same ns twice) → 2 identical queries.
  - `-q a.com -q b.com -t A -t MX` → order: `a.com A`, `a.com MX`, `b.com A`,
    `b.com MX` (domain-major, type-minor).
  - `-U -T` → 2 queries over different transports, flag order preserved.
- Each query gets its own random txid unless `--txid` pins them all.
- Default query (no `-Z`, no `--edns`): flags `0x0100` (RD only), QDCOUNT=1,
  one OPT additional (type 41, UDP payload 512, TTL 0, no options). Example
  full wire bytes of `dog example.com @127.0.0.1:5510` (txid random, here 0xb046):

  `b046 0100 0001 0000 0000 0001 076578616d706c6503636f6d00 0001 0001 0000290200000000000000`

---

## 6. Message/catalog reference (verbatim, all end with `\n`)

stderr, exit 3, prefix `dog: Invalid options: `:
- `Unrecognized option: 'frobnicate'`
- `Unrecognized option: 'x'`
- `Unrecognized option: 'typ'`
- `Unrecognized option: 'foo'` (from `--foo=bar`)
- `Unrecognized option: 'h'` / `'V'`
- `Argument to option 'type' missing` (also `t`, `q`, `query`, `n`, `nameserver`, `class`, `edns`, `txid`, `Z`, `colour`)
- `Option 'udp' does not take an argument`
- `Option 'help' does not take an argument`
- `Option 'txid' given more than once` (also `edns`, `udp`, `time`, `seconds`, `short`, `json`)
- `Invalid query type "FOO"` / `"=MX"` / `"-T"` / `""` / `"65536"` / `"-1"` / `"0x10"` / `"*"` / `"DNSKEY"` / `"SVCB"`
- `Invalid query class "XX"` / `"ANY"` / `"NONE"` / `""` / `"65536"` / `"-1"`
- `Invalid transaction ID "abc"` / `"65536"` / `"-1"` / `""` / `" 5"` / `"5 "` / `"0X10"` / `"99999999999999999999"`
- `Invalid EDNS setting "bogus"` / `"DISABLE"` / `"example.com"` / `""`
- `Invalid protocol tweak "bogus"` / `"AA"` / `"aa,ad"` / `"bufsize=abc"` / `"bufsize=99999"` / `"bufsize=-1"` / `"=aa"` / `""`
- `OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)` (for `-t OPT` or plain `OPT`)
- `Invalid domain "-T"` / `"-J"` / `"-"`

stderr, exit 1, prefix `Error [network]: `:
- `Network is unreachable (os error 101)`
- `Connection refused (os error 111)`
- `Address family not supported by protocol (os error 97)`
- `failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`
- `invalid port value`

Panic (exit 134): see §3 `-H`.

## 7. Surprises worth highlighting

1. `--version` output contains a stray literal `m` before the URL
   (`mhttps://dns.lookup.dog/`).
2. No-domain invocations print the full help to **stdout** with exit **3**
   (not an error message, not stderr).
3. Invalid `--color` values are silently ignored (treated as `automatic`);
   `--color` always overrides `--colour` irrespective of position.
4. `-U -T` doesn't conflict — transports accumulate and multiple queries run;
   partial transport failure → exit 1 even though answers were printed.
5. `-H` with a non-URL nameserver **panics** (SIGABRT, exit 134).
6. `--txid` accepts lowercase `0x` hex and `+N`; `-t`/`--class` numerics do
   not accept hex. Nothing is whitespace-trimmed.
7. `DNSKEY`, `SVCB`, `HTTPS`, `SPF` are NOT known types (become domains);
   `DLV`, `TA`, `EUI48`, `DHCID` are.
8. Domain args are lowercased and punycode-encoded; `-q` values too; `-n`
   values are used verbatim (`@` not stripped).
9. `--` stops option parsing but plain-argument guessing still applies.
10. `OPT` as a type is refused with a dedicated message pointing at `-Z`.

```

- `--version example.com` / `-v -T` → version printed, exit 0 (short-circuits).
- `--version --frobnicate` → exit 3, unrecognized-option error (parse errors
  take precedence over both `--version` and `--help`, regardless of order).
- `-h` and `-V` are NOT aliases: `dog: Invalid options: Unrecognized option: 'h'` (exit 3).

---

## 2. Option syntax rules (getopts-style)

- Long options accept `--opt=value` **and** `--opt value` (next argument is
  consumed as the value, even if it looks like data: `--edns example.com`
  consumes `example.com` as the EDNS value → `Invalid EDNS setting "example.com"`).
- `--color` also consumes the next token even if it looks like a flag:
  `--color -1 example.com ...` → `-1` is the color value (invalid → ignored),
  so short mode is NOT active.
- Short options accept attached values: `-tMX`, `-qexample.com`, `-Zaa`,
  `-Zbufsize=512` all work. `-t=MX` → value is literally `=MX`
  → `Invalid query type "=MX"`. `-Z=aa` → `Invalid protocol tweak "=aa"`.
- Short flags cluster: `-1J`, `-J1`, `-UT`, `-U1J` all work. In a cluster a
  value-taking option consumes the rest of the cluster: `-1tMX` = `-1 -t MX`;
  `-1t MX` = `-1 -t MX` too.
- No long-option abbreviation: `--typ MX` → `Unrecognized option: 'typ'`.
- Unknown options: `--frobnicate` → `Unrecognized option: 'frobnicate'`;
  `-x` → `Unrecognized option: 'x'`; `-1x` → `Unrecognized option: 'x'`;
  `--foo=bar` → `Unrecognized option: 'foo'` (value not shown);
  `--foo-bar` → `Unrecognized option: 'foo-bar'`.
- A flag given a value: `--udp=true` → `Option 'udp' does not take an argument`;
  `--help=foo` → `Option 'help' does not take an argument`.
- Missing value (option last on the line): `dog: Invalid options: Argument to option 'X' missing`
  where X is the option as spelled: `t`, `type`, `q`, `query`, `n`, `nameserver`,
  `class`, `edns`, `txid`, `Z`, `colour`. (Verified for `--type`, `-t`,
  `--edns`, `--class`, `--txid`, `-Z`, `--query`, `-n`, `--colour`.)
- A value-taking option followed by another flag consumes that flag as its
  value: `-t -T example.com` → `Invalid query type "-T"`.
- All argument errors go to **stderr**, exact prefix `dog: Invalid options: `,
  one line, trailing `\n`, exit **`3`**, nothing on stdout (except the
  no-domain case which prints help to stdout).

### `--` separator
- Everything after `--` is a plain argument, but **guessing still applies**:
  `example.com -- MX @ns` and `-- example.com MX @ns` still treat `MX` as a
  type and `@ns` as a nameserver (wire: qtype 15).
- A plain argument starting with `-` is rejected:
  `dog -- -T` → `Invalid domain "-T"`; `-1 -- -J example.com` →
  `Invalid domain "-J"`; `dog - example.com` → `Invalid domain "-"`.
  (Exit 3 in all cases.)

### Duplicates
- Repeatable (accumulate): `-q/--query`, `-t/--type`, `-n/--nameserver`,
  `--class`, `-Z`. Repeated values produce multiple queries (see §5).
  `-Z aa -Z aa` is fine.
- Not repeatable — second occurrence → exit 3,
  `dog: Invalid options: Option 'X' given more than once` where X is the long
  name. Verified: `txid`, `edns`, `udp` (`-U -U` or `-U --udp`), `time`,
  `seconds`, `short` (`-1 -1`), `json` (`-J -J`).
- `--color` + `--colour` together do NOT error (see §6).

---

## 3. Value validation (all exit 3 on failure, message format given)

### `-t, --type=TYPE`
Accepted, case-insensitively (`mx`, `Mx`, `iXfR` work), the following 41
names — same set as the plain-argument guesser:

| name | num | name | num | name | num |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 | NS | 2 | CNAME | 5 |
| SOA | 6 | PTR | 12 | HINFO | 13 |
| MX | 15 | TXT | 16 | RP | 17 |
| AFSDB | 18 | KEY | 25 | AAAA | 28 |
| LOC | 29 | SRV | 33 | NAPTR | 35 |
| KX | 36 | DNAME | 39 | APL | 42 |
| DS | 43 | RRSIG | 46 | NSEC | 47 |
| DHCID | 49 | NSEC3 | 50 | NSEC3PARAM | 51 |
| TLSA | 52 | CDNSKEY | 60 | CDS | 59 |
| OPENPGPKEY | 61 | EUI48 | 108 | EUI64 | 109 |
| TKEY | 249 | TSIG | 250 | IXFR | 251 |
| AXFR | 252 | ANY | 255 | URI | 256 |
| CAA | 257 | TA | 32768 | DLV | 32769 |

(SSHFP=44 is also accepted — verified via plain arg; full accepted set:
A AAAA AFSDB ANY APL AXFR CAA CDNSKEY CDS CNAME DHCID DLV DNAME DS EUI48
EUI64 HINFO IXFR KEY KX LOC MX NAPTR NS NSEC NSEC3 NSEC3PARAM OPENPGPKEY PTR
RP RRSIG SOA SRV SSHFP TA TKEY TLSA TSIG TXT URI.)

- Also accepted: decimal numbers `0`–`65535` (`-t 0`, `-t 1`, `-t 255`,
  `-t 65535` all sent on the wire; `+1` and `01` accepted).
- Rejected (`dog: Invalid options: Invalid query type "X"`, exit 3):
  any unknown name (`FOO`, `DNSKEY`, `SVCB`, `HTTPS`, `SPF`, `ZONEMD`,
  `WKS`, `MD`, `MF`, `MB`, `MG`, `MR`, `MINFO`, `NULL`, `MAILA`, `MAILB`,
  `ALL`, `NONE` — note DNSKEY/SVCB/HTTPS are **not** known!), `65536`, `-1`,
  `0x10`, `*` (and shell glob `*`), empty string (`Invalid query type ""`).
- `OPT` is special: `Invalid query type "OPT"`? No — as an explicit `-t OPT`
  or plain arg it yields: `dog: Invalid options: OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)`.
- Validation happens before any network: `-t FOO example.com` → exit 3, no query.

### `--class=CLASS`
- Accepted case-insensitively: `IN`=1, `CH`=3, `HS`=4 (`--class=ch` works).
- Accepted numerically: `0`–`65535` (`--class=0`, `--class=1`,
  `--class=65535`, `+1`, `01` OK).
- Rejected: `ANY`, `NONE`, `none`, `XX`, `65536`, `-1`, empty →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "X"`.

### `--txid=NUMBER`
- Accepted: `0`–`65535` decimal, plus `+5` (→5), leading zeros (`0007`→7),
  and **hex with lowercase `0x` prefix** (`0x10`→16). Verified on the wire
  (`0005…`, `0010…`, `ffff…` as first two bytes).
- Rejected: `65536`, `-1`, `abc`, `0X10` (capital X!), ` 5`, `5 ` (no
  trimming), empty, huge numbers →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "X"`.
- Given more than once → `Option 'txid' given more than once`.
- One `--txid` applies to ALL queries when multiple are sent (both queries
  used txid 42).

### `--edns=SETTING`
- Accepted (case-SENSITIVE, lowercase only): `disable`, `hide`, `show`.
- `disable` → no OPT record in the query (ARCOUNT=0).
- `hide` and `show` → byte-identical queries (OPT record, UDP payload 512);
  they differ only in output rendering.
- Rejected: `bogus`, `DISABLE`, `` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid EDNS setting "X"`.

### `-Z=TWEAKS` (repeatable; each `-Z` takes exactly ONE tweak)
- `aa` → sets AA bit (flags 0x0500 with RD). `ad` → 0x0120. `cd` → 0x0110.
  Combined `-Z aa -Z ad -Z cd` → flags 0x0530.
- `bufsize=NUM` → sets OPT UDP payload size (`bufsize=1024` → 0x0400,
  `bufsize=4096` → 0x1000, `bufsize=0` → 0x0000). Range 0–65535;
  `bufsize=99999`, `bufsize=-1`, `bufsize=abc` →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "bufsize=99999"` etc.
- Case-sensitive: `-Z AA` → `Invalid protocol tweak "AA"`.
- No comma syntax: `-Z aa,ad` → `Invalid protocol tweak "aa,ad"`.
- Any other value (e.g. `bogus`, `example.com`, `=aa`, empty) →
  `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "X"`.

### `--color, --colour=WHEN`
- Accepted values: `always`, `automatic`, `never` (case-sensitive in effect;
  see below). Both spellings are the same option family, but...
- **Surprise 1:** invalid values are silently accepted — no error, exit
  unaffected. `--color=bogus`, `--color=ALWAYS` behave like `automatic`
  (no color when stdout is not a TTY).
- **Surprise 2:** when both spellings are given, `--color` wins over
  `--colour` **regardless of order**: `--color=never --colour=always` → no
  color; `--colour=always --color=never` → no color; `--color=always
  --colour=never` → color. (i.e. `--colour` is only a fallback used when
  `--color` is absent.)
- `--color always` (space form) works and colorizes.
- `always` with piped stdout produced: `^[[1;32mA^[[0m ^[[1;34mexample.com.^[[0m 5m00s   1.2.3.4`
  (type bold green `1;32`, name bold blue `1;34`, reset `0`).

### Conflicting / combined output & protocol options
- `-1` + `-J` (either order, incl. clusters `-1J`/`-J1`): **short mode wins**;
  output is just `1.2.3.4\n`, exit 0. No error.
- `-U -T` / `-T -U` / `-UT`: **no error — protocols accumulate**, one query
  per transport, in the order the flags were given. Against a TCP-only server:
  `-U -T` printed `Error [network]: Connection refused (os error 111)` (stderr)
  then the answer (stdout), exit **1**; `-T -U` printed the answer then the
  error, exit **1**. Against a dual-stack server both succeed and the answer
  table is printed twice, exit 0.
- `-S` (TLS) to a plain-TCP server **hangs** (no data ever arrives; killed by
  `timeout`, exit 124). `-T -S` likewise hangs on the TLS leg.
- `-H` with a non-URL nameserver (e.g. `example.com -H @127.0.0.1:5510`):
  **panics**. stderr exactly (PID varies; the final line about core dump comes
  from `timeout`, not dog):
  ```
  \nthread 'main' (7937) panicked at dns-transport/src/https.rs:42:50:\nInvalid HTTPS nameserver\nnote: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n
  ```
  Exit **134** (SIGABRT, core dumped).
- `-H -n https://127.0.0.1:5512/dns-query example.com` → no panic, but exit 1
  with `Error [network]: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`
  (observed in this offline env).

---

## 4. Plain-argument guessing rules

Every non-option argument (including those after `--`) is classified by the
first matching rule:

1. **Starts with `@`** → nameserver. The remainder is parsed as
   `host`, `host:port`, `[v6addr]`, `[v6addr]:port`. Details:
   - `@127.0.0.1:5510` works (port parsed numerically).
   - `@1.2.3.4:5510` → tries that IP (exit 1 `Network is unreachable (os error 101)` offline).
   - `@[::1]:5510` → parsed as IPv6; exit 1 `Address family not supported by protocol (os error 97)` here.
   - `@::1` (bare v6, no brackets) → NOT parsed as IPv6; treated as a hostname
     for the OS resolver → `Error [network]: failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`, exit 1.
   - `@localhost:5510` → works (OS resolves `localhost`; dog does not resolve it itself).
   - `@` alone, `@-foo` → hostname lookup fails: same `failed to lookup address information` error, exit 1.
   - `@127.0.0.1:` or `@127.0.0.1:abc` → `Error [network]: invalid port value`, exit 1.
   - `@127.0.0.1:0` → connects to port 0 → `Connection refused (os error 111)`.
   - `@https://127.0.0.1:5512/dns-query` → `Error [network]: invalid port value`, exit 1 (plain @URL does not switch to HTTPS).
   - These are runtime/network errors (exit 1), not argument errors (exit 3).
2. **Case-insensitive match of a known TYPE name** (the 41-name list in §3,
   e.g. `A`, `a`, `MX`, `any`, `iXfR`) → query type. `OPT` → the special
   `OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)` error.
3. **Case-insensitive match of `IN`, `CH`, `HS`** → query class.
4. **Anything else** → domain name. This includes: unknown uppercase words
   (`FOO` → qname `foo`), unknown type-like strings (`DNSKEY`, `SVCB`,
   `HTTPS`, `ALL`, `NONE`, `NULL`, `WKS`...), pure numbers (`123`, `255`,
   `15` → qnames `123`, `255`, `15`), IPv4-looking strings (`1.2.3.4` →
   qname `1.2.3.4`), bare IPv6 (`::1` → qname literally `::1`, one label),
   names with hyphens/underscores (`my-host.example.com`,
   `_dmarc.example.com`), weird TLDs (`example.xyzzy`), trailing dots
   (`example.com.` → sent as `example.com`), `mx.`/`in.` (trailing dot
   defeats type/class matching → domains `mx`, `in`), empty string `` and
   `.` (both → root qname, zero labels).
5. Plain args starting with `-` → `Invalid domain "X"`, exit 3.

Domain normalization (applies to plain domains AND `-q` values):
- **Lowercased**: `ExAmPle.CoM` and `-q ExAmPle.COM` → wire qname `example.com`.
- **IDNA/punycode-encoded**: `bücher.de` → `xn--bcher-kva.de` on the wire.

Explicit options bypass guessing:
- `-q @foo` → qname literally `@foo` (one label), not a nameserver.
- `-n @127.0.0.1:5510` → the `@` is NOT stripped; `@127.0.0.1` goes to the OS
  resolver → `failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`, exit 1.
- `-q ''` → root query (zero-label qname).

A run needs ≥1 domain: if the args contain only types/classes/nameservers
(`dog A @127.0.0.1:5510`, `dog IN @ns`, `dog @ns`), help is printed to stdout,
exit 3.

---

## 5. Multiple values → cross-product queries

- Repeating `-q`, `-t`, `-n`, `--class` (or mixing plain and explicit values)
  accumulates lists; dog sends one query per combination. Verified:
  - `-q a.com -q b.com @ns` → 2 queries (a.com, b.com).
  - `-t A -t MX example.com` → 2 queries (A then MX).
  - `--class=IN --class=CH` → qclass 1 then 3. `example.com CH HS` → same.
  - `-n ns -n ns example.com` (same ns twice) → 2 identical queries.
  - `-q a.com -q b.com -t A -t MX` → order: `a.com A`, `a.com MX`, `b.com A`,
    `b.com MX` (domain-major, type-minor).
  - `-U -T` → 2 queries over different transports, flag order preserved.
- Each query gets its own random txid unless `--txid` pins them all.
- Default query (no `-Z`, no `--edns`): flags `0x0100` (RD only), QDCOUNT=1,
  one OPT additional (type 41, UDP payload 512, TTL 0, no options). Example
  full wire bytes of `dog example.com @127.0.0.1:5510` (txid random, here 0xb046):

  `b046 0100 0001 0000 0000 0001 076578616d706c6503636f6d00 0001 0001 0000290200000000000000`

---

## 6. Message/catalog reference (verbatim, all end with `\n`)

stderr, exit 3, prefix `dog: Invalid options: `:
- `Unrecognized option: 'frobnicate'`
- `Unrecognized option: 'x'`
- `Unrecognized option: 'typ'`
- `Unrecognized option: 'foo'` (from `--foo=bar`)
- `Unrecognized option: 'h'` / `'V'`
- `Argument to option 'type' missing` (also `t`, `q`, `query`, `n`, `nameserver`, `class`, `edns`, `txid`, `Z`, `colour`)
- `Option 'udp' does not take an argument`
- `Option 'help' does not take an argument`
- `Option 'txid' given more than once` (also `edns`, `udp`, `time`, `seconds`, `short`, `json`)
- `Invalid query type "FOO"` / `"=MX"` / `"-T"` / `""` / `"65536"` / `"-1"` / `"0x10"` / `"*"` / `"DNSKEY"` / `"SVCB"`
- `Invalid query class "XX"` / `"ANY"` / `"NONE"` / `""` / `"65536"` / `"-1"`
- `Invalid transaction ID "abc"` / `"65536"` / `"-1"` / `""` / `" 5"` / `"5 "` / `"0X10"` / `"99999999999999999999"`
- `Invalid EDNS setting "bogus"` / `"DISABLE"` / `"example.com"` / `""`
- `Invalid protocol tweak "bogus"` / `"AA"` / `"aa,ad"` / `"bufsize=abc"` / `"bufsize=99999"` / `"bufsize=-1"` / `"=aa"` / `""`
- `OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)` (for `-t OPT` or plain `OPT`)
- `Invalid domain "-T"` / `"-J"` / `"-"`

stderr, exit 1, prefix `Error [network]: `:
- `Network is unreachable (os error 101)`
- `Connection refused (os error 111)`
- `Address family not supported by protocol (os error 97)`
- `failed to lookup address information: Name or service not known`
- `invalid port value`

Panic (exit 134): see §3 `-H`.

## 7. Surprises worth highlighting

1. `--version` output contains a stray literal `m` before the URL
   (`mhttps://dns.lookup.dog/`).
2. No-domain invocations print the full help to **stdout** with exit **3**
   (not an error message, not stderr).
3. Invalid `--color` values are silently ignored (treated as `automatic`);
   `--color` always overrides `--colour` irrespective of position.
4. `-U -T` doesn't conflict — transports accumulate and multiple queries run;
   partial transport failure → exit 1 even though answers were printed.
5. `-H` with a non-URL nameserver **panics** (SIGABRT, exit 134).
6. `--txid` accepts lowercase `0x` hex and `+N`; `-t`/`--class` numerics do
   not accept hex. Nothing is whitespace-trimmed.
7. `DNSKEY`, `SVCB`, `HTTPS`, `SPF` are NOT known types (become domains);
   `DLV`, `TA`, `EUI48`, `DHCID` are.
8. Domain args are lowercased and punycode-encoded; `-q` values too; `-n`
   values are used verbatim (`@` not stripped).
9. `--` stops option parsing but plain-argument guessing still applies.
10. `OPT` as a type is refused with a dedicated message pointing at `-Z`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""LOC rendering math sweep."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

EQ = 2**31

def latenc(deg, m, s_ms, neg=False):
    v = ((deg * 60 + m) * 60 * 1000) + s_ms
    return EQ - v if neg else EQ + v

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    # equator / prime meridian, alt 0, size 0x12 (100cm), hp 0x16, vp 0x13
    r.add_answer("l0.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000))
    # 52 12 34.000 N, 0 7 23.000 E, alt 10m
    r.add_answer("l1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 latenc(52, 12, 34000), latenc(0, 7, 23000), 10000000 + 1000))
    # south/west: 33 51 35.9 S, 151 12 40.5 W, alt -10m
    r.add_answer("l2.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 latenc(33, 51, 35900, True), latenc(151, 12, 40500, True), 10000000 - 1000))
    # max-ish: 89 59 59.999 N, 179 59 59.999 E, alt 89999.99m
    r.add_answer("l3.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 latenc(89, 59, 59999), latenc(179, 59, 59999), 10000000 + 8999999))
    # alt negative big: -100000m (encoded 0)
    r.add_answer("l4.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 0))
    # size/hp/vp byte variations: 0x00, 0x10, 0x29, 0x99, 0x13
    for i, s in enumerate([0x00, 0x10, 0x29, 0x99, 0x13]):
        r.add_answer(f"s{i}.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, s, s, s, EQ, EQ, 10000000))
    # fractional seconds
    r.add_answer("l5.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 latenc(1, 2, 3456), latenc(4, 5, 6789), 10000000 + 12345))
    # version 1
    r.add_answer("v1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(1, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000))
    return r

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(handler, port=int(sys.argv[1]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Silent UDP server: logs query arrival times, never responds."""
import sys, socket, time
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import parse_query

port = int(sys.argv[1])
u = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
u.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
u.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
t0 = time.time()
print("silent server up", flush=True)
while True:
    data, addr = u.recvfrom(65535)
    print(f"{time.time()-t0:7.3f}s txid={parse_query(data)['txid']}", flush=True)

args.content:
# Spec: query-wire — exact bytes dog sends on the wire

Probed by running `/workspace/executable` against fake DNS servers on
127.0.0.1 ports 5513–5519 that dump every received query as raw hex
(scripts: `/workspace/probe/querywire_server.py`, `/workspace/probe/querywire_tc.py`).
All invocations were wrapped in `timeout 10`.

---

## 1. Default query packet

Command: `./executable example.com @127.0.0.1:5513` (exit 0)

Raw bytes received over UDP (txid varies, here `0xee08`):

```
ee08 0100 0001 0000 0000 0001                      header
07 6578616d706c65 03 636f6d 00                     qname "example.com"
0001 0001                                          qtype=A(1) qclass=IN(1)
00 0029 0200 00000000 0000                         OPT record (additional)
```

Header fields:

- **txid**: random 16-bit, fresh per query (see §2).
- **flags**: `0x0100` — only RD set. QR=0, opcode=0, AA=0, TC=0, RA=0, Z=0,
  AD=0, CD=0, rcode=0. There is no way to clear RD (`-Z rd` is rejected).
- **QDCOUNT=1, ANCOUNT=0, NSCOUNT=0, ARCOUNT=1**.
- Exactly one question per packet; multiple domains/types/classes produce
  multiple separate packets (§6).

EDNS OPT pseudo-record (always present by default):

- NAME = root (`00`)
- TYPE = 41 (`0x0029`)
- CLASS = **512** (`0x0200`) — UDP payload size
- TTL = `0x00000000` — extended-rcode 0, EDNS version 0, flags `0x0000`
  (DO bit NOT set)
- RDLENGTH = 0, no options

Total length for `example.com`: 40 bytes (`0x28`).

---

## 2. Transaction ID

- Default: a fresh random 16-bit value per query. Two consecutive runs gave
  60936 then 8351; within one run of 4 queries, all 4 txids differ.
- `--txid=N` sets the exact value, big-endian. `--txid=4660` → bytes `1234`;
  `--txid=0` → `0000`; `--txid=65535` → `ffff`.
- With `--txid` and multiple queries, the SAME txid is reused for every query
  (observed `--txid=1 A MX example.com` → both packets have txid `0001`,
  also over TCP).
- Invalid values print to stderr and exit **3**:
  - `--txid=65536` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "65536"`
  - `--txid=abc`   → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "abc"`
  - `--txid=-1`    → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "-1"`

---

## 3. `-Z` protocol tweaks

`-Z` takes ONE tweak per occurrence; repeat the flag to combine.
`-Z "aa ad"` (space-separated) is rejected.

Wire effects (base flags are `0x0100`):

| invocation | flags word | OPT class |
|---|---|---|
| (default) | `0x0100` | 512 (`0x0200`) |
| `-Z aa` | `0x0500` (sets AA bit 0x0400 in the *query*) | 512 |
| `-Z ad` | `0x0120` (AD bit 0x0020) | 512 |
| `-Z cd` | `0x0110` (CD bit 0x0010) | 512 |
| `-Z bufsize=4096` | `0x0100` | 4096 (`0x1000`) |
| `-Z bufsize=0` | `0x0100` | 0 |
| `-Z bufsize=65535` | `0x0100` | 65535 (`0xffff`) |
| `-Z bufsize=08` | `0x0100` | 8 (leading zeros OK) |
| `-Z aa -Z cd` | `0x0510` | 512 |
| `-Z aa -Z ad -Z cd -Z bufsize=1232` | `0x0530` | 1232 |

`bufsize` only changes the OPT CLASS field; the OPT record is otherwise
unchanged. With `--edns=disable`, `bufsize` has no effect (no OPT sent).

Errors (stderr, exit **3**), message shows the whole tweak token:

- `-Z bogus` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "bogus"`
- `-Z rd` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "rd"`
- `-Z AA` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "AA"` (case-sensitive)
- `-Z "aa ad"` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "aa ad"`
- `-Z bufsize=abc` / `bufsize=65536` / `bufsize=-1` / `bufsize=` /
  `bufsize= 100` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "<token>"`

---

## 4. `--edns=disable|hide|show`

Wire effect (query for `example.com A`, 29 vs 40 bytes):

- `--edns=disable`: NO OPT record; ARCOUNT=0. Full packet hex:
  `1eb2 0100 0001 0000 0000 0000 076578616d706c6503636f6d00 0001 0001`
- `--edns=hide`: **identical to the default** — OPT present, payload 512.
- `--edns=show`: identical to default on the wire as well.

`hide` vs `show` is a display-side distinction, but in this build no
difference could be observed in output either: a response containing a
well-formed root-named OPT additional (payload 4096, DO bit, one COOKIE
option) renders exactly the same under `hide`, `show`, `disable`, and
default — the OPT record is simply never shown in text or `-J` output
(`"additionals":[]`).

`--edns=disable -Z bufsize=4096` → still no OPT (bufsize is inert).
`--edns=hide -Z bufsize=4096` → OPT with class 4096.

Errors (stderr, exit **3**, case-sensitive):

- `--edns=bogus` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid EDNS setting "bogus"`
- `--edns=DISABLE` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid EDNS setting "DISABLE"`

---

## 5. Query types (`-t` / `--type` / plain argument)

Type matching is **case-insensitive** (`-t a`, `-t Aaaa`, `-t tXt` all work).
Bare **numbers** are also accepted: `-t 0`, `-t 1`, `-t 28`, `-t 255`,
`-t 65535` all send that qtype verbatim (qtype 0 is allowed!).
Rejected: `-t -1`, `-t 99999` (>65535), `-t TYPE1` (no TYPE#### syntax).

Complete list of accepted type names and their wire qtype numbers
(each verified on the wire; everything not listed here was rejected —
46 names accepted out of 82 common names tried):

| name | qtype | | name | qtype | | name | qtype |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 | | DNAME | 39 | | CSYNC | 62 |
| NS | 2 | | APL | 42 | | EUI48 | 108 |
| CNAME | 5 | | DS | 43 | | EUI64 | 109 |
| SOA | 6 | | SSHFP | 44 | | TKEY | 249 |
| PTR | 12 | | IPSECKEY | 45 | | TSIG | 250 |
| HINFO | 13 | | RRSIG | 46 | | IXFR | 251 |
| MX | 15 | | NSEC | 47 | | AXFR | 252 |
| TXT | 16 | | DHCID | 49 | | ANY | 255 |
| RP | 17 | | NSEC3 | 50 | | URI | 256 |
| AFSDB | 18 | | NSEC3PARAM | 51 | | CAA | 257 |
| SIG | 24 | | TLSA | 52 | | TA | 32768 |
| KEY | 25 | | SMIMEA | 53 | | DLV | 32769 |
| AAAA | 28 | | HIP | 55 | | | |
| LOC | 29 | | CDS | 59 | | | |
| SRV | 33 | | CDNSKEY | 60 | | | |
| NAPTR | 35 | | OPENPGPKEY | 61 | | | |
| KX | 36 | | | | | | |
| CERT | 37 | | | | | | |

Notable: `DNSKEY` is NOT accepted (but `CDS`/`CDNSKEY` are). `SVCB`,
`HTTPS`, `SPF`, `NINFO`, `ZONEMD`, `AVC`, `DOA`, `MAILA`, `MAILB`, `NULL`,
`WKS`, `MD`, `MF`, etc. are all rejected.

Special case — `-t OPT` is rejected with a UNIQUE message (exit 3):
`dog: Invalid options: OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)`

All other unknown names (stderr, exit **3**):
`dog: Invalid options: Invalid query type "NAME"` (NAME echoed as typed).

Plain (non-flag) arguments that match a type name are treated as types:
`dog MX example.com`, `dog mx example.com`, `dog any example.com`,
`dog A example.com` all work; argument order is free
(`dog example.com MX` == `dog MX example.com`). A bare numeric plain
argument is NOT a type: `dog 123 @...` queries domain `123` with qtype A.

---

## 6. Query classes (`--class` / plain argument)

- Names case-insensitive: `IN`→1, `CH`→3, `HS`→4 (`--class in`, `ch`, `hs` ok).
- Bare numbers accepted: `--class 0`→0, `--class 1`, `--class 3`,
  `--class 65535` all sent verbatim.
- Rejected (stderr, exit **3**):
  - `--class Chaos` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "Chaos"`
  - `--class NONE` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "NONE"`
  - `--class ANY` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "ANY"`
  - `--class 65536` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "65536"`
  - `--class XX` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "XX"`
- Plain args `IN`/`CH`/`HS` (any case) are detected as classes:
  `dog CH example.com` sends qclass 3.

---

## 7. Domain-name encoding

The qname is transformed before encoding:

- **Lowercased**: `Example.COM`, `EXAMPLE.COM.`, `WWW.Example.ORG` all go
  on the wire lowercase (`07777777...` → `03777777076578616d706c65036f726700`
  = "www.example.org").
- **IDNA/punycode**: `bücher.de` → `xn--bcher-kva.de`
  (`0d 786e2d2d62636865722d6b7661 02 6465 00`); `BÜCHER.DE` → same
  (lowercase + punycode). Already-punycode `xn--bcher-kva.de` passes through.
- **Trailing dot ignored**: `example.com.` ≡ `example.com` (same bytes).
- **Leading dot stripped**: `.example.com` → `example.com`.
- **Empty labels collapsed**: `a..b.com` → `a.b.com`; `example..com` →
  `example.com`.
- Root: `.` → qname `00` (queries the root, qtype A).
- Single labels fine: `localhost` → `09 6c6f63616c686f7374 00`.

# Spec: query-wire — exact bytes dog sends on the wire

Probed by running `/workspace/executable` against fake DNS servers on
127.0.0.1 ports 5513–5519 that dump every received query as raw hex
(scripts: `/workspace/probe/querywire_server.py`, `/workspace/probe/querywire_tc.py`).
All invocations were wrapped in `timeout 10`.

---

## 1. Default query packet

Command: `./executable example.com @127.0.0.1:5513` (exit 0)

Raw bytes received over UDP (txid varies, here `0xee08`):

```
ee08 0100 0001 0000 0000 0001                      header
07 6578616d706c65 03 636f6d 00                     qname "example.com"
0001 0001                                          qtype=A(1) qclass=IN(1)
00 0029 0200 00000000 0000                         OPT record (additional)
```

Header fields:

- **txid**: random 16-bit, fresh per query (see §2).
- **flags**: `0x0100` — only RD set. QR=0, opcode=0, AA=0, TC=0, RA=0, Z=0,
  AD=0, CD=0, rcode=0. There is no way to clear RD (`-Z rd` is rejected).
- **QDCOUNT=1, ANCOUNT=0, NSCOUNT=0, ARCOUNT=1**.
- Exactly one question per packet; multiple domains/types/classes produce
  multiple separate packets (§6).

EDNS OPT pseudo-record (always present by default):

- NAME = root (`00`)
- TYPE = 41 (`0x0029`)
- CLASS = **512** (`0x0200`) — UDP payload size
- TTL = `0x00000000` — extended-rcode 0, EDNS version 0, flags `0x0000`
  (DO bit NOT set)
- RDLENGTH = 0, no options

Total length for `example.com`: 40 bytes (`0x28`).

---

## 2. Transaction ID

- Default: a fresh random 16-bit value per query. Two consecutive runs gave
  60936 then 8351; within one run of 4 queries, all 4 txids differ.
- `--txid=N` sets the exact value, big-endian. `--txid=4660` → bytes `1234`;
  `--txid=0` → `0000`; `--txid=65535` → `ffff`.
- With `--txid` and multiple queries, the SAME txid is reused for every query
  (observed `--txid=1 A MX example.com` → both packets have txid `0001`,
  also over TCP).
- Invalid values print to stderr and exit **3**:
  - `--txid=65536` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "65536"`
  - `--txid=abc`   → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "abc"`
  - `--txid=-1`    → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "-1"`

---

## 3. `-Z` protocol tweaks

`-Z` takes ONE tweak per occurrence; repeat the flag to combine.
`-Z "aa ad"` (space-separated) is rejected.

Wire effects (base flags are `0x0100`):

| invocation | flags word | OPT class |
|---|---|---|
| (default) | `0x0100` | 512 (`0x0200`) |
| `-Z aa` | `0x0500` (sets AA bit 0x0400 in the *query*) | 512 |
| `-Z ad` | `0x0120` (AD bit 0x0020) | 512 |
| `-Z cd` | `0x0110` (CD bit 0x0010) | 512 |
| `-Z bufsize=4096` | `0x0100` | 4096 (`0x1000`) |
| `-Z bufsize=0` | `0x0100` | 0 |
| `-Z bufsize=65535` | `0x0100` | 65535 (`0xffff`) |
| `-Z bufsize=08` | `0x0100` | 8 (leading zeros OK) |
| `-Z aa -Z cd` | `0x0510` | 512 |
| `-Z aa -Z ad -Z cd -Z bufsize=1232` | `0x0530` | 1232 |

`bufsize` only changes the OPT CLASS field; the OPT record is otherwise
unchanged. With `--edns=disable`, `bufsize` has no effect (no OPT sent).

Errors (stderr, exit **3**), message shows the whole tweak token:

- `-Z bogus` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "bogus"`
- `-Z rd` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "rd"`
- `-Z AA` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "AA"` (case-sensitive)
- `-Z "aa ad"` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "aa ad"`
- `-Z bufsize=abc` / `bufsize=65536` / `bufsize=-1` / `bufsize=` /
  `bufsize= 100` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid protocol tweak "<token>"`

---

## 4. `--edns=disable|hide|show`

Wire effect (query for `example.com A`, 29 vs 40 bytes):

- `--edns=disable`: NO OPT record; ARCOUNT=0. Full packet hex:
  `1eb2 0100 0001 0000 0000 0000 076578616d706c6503636f6d00 0001 0001`
- `--edns=hide`: **identical to the default** — OPT present, payload 512.
- `--edns=show`: identical to default on the wire as well.

`hide` vs `show` is a display-side distinction, but in this build no
difference could be observed in output either: a response containing a
well-formed root-named OPT additional (payload 4096, DO bit, one COOKIE
option) renders exactly the same under `hide`, `show`, `disable`, and
default — the OPT record is simply never shown in text or `-J` output
(`"additionals":[]`).

`--edns=disable -Z bufsize=4096` → still no OPT (bufsize is inert).
`--edns=hide -Z bufsize=4096` → OPT with class 4096.

Errors (stderr, exit **3**, case-sensitive):

- `--edns=bogus` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid EDNS setting "bogus"`
- `--edns=DISABLE` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid EDNS setting "DISABLE"`

---

## 5. Query types (`-t` / `--type` / plain argument)

Type matching is **case-insensitive** (`-t a`, `-t Aaaa`, `-t tXt` all work).
Bare **numbers** are also accepted: `-t 0`, `-t 1`, `-t 28`, `-t 255`,
`-t 65535` all send that qtype verbatim (qtype 0 is allowed!).
Rejected: `-t -1`, `-t 99999` (>65535), `-t TYPE1` (no TYPE#### syntax).

Complete list of accepted type names and their wire qtype numbers
(each verified on the wire; everything not listed here was rejected —
46 names accepted out of 82 common names tried):

| name | qtype | | name | qtype | | name | qtype |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1 | | DNAME | 39 | | CSYNC | 62 |
| NS | 2 | | APL | 42 | | EUI48 | 108 |
| CNAME | 5 | | DS | 43 | | EUI64 | 109 |
| SOA | 6 | | SSHFP | 44 | | TKEY | 249 |
| PTR | 12 | | IPSECKEY | 45 | | TSIG | 250 |
| HINFO | 13 | | RRSIG | 46 | | IXFR | 251 |
| MX | 15 | | NSEC | 47 | | AXFR | 252 |
| TXT | 16 | | DHCID | 49 | | ANY | 255 |
| RP | 17 | | NSEC3 | 50 | | URI | 256 |
| AFSDB | 18 | | NSEC3PARAM | 51 | | CAA | 257 |
| SIG | 24 | | TLSA | 52 | | TA | 32768 |
| KEY | 25 | | SMIMEA | 53 | | DLV | 32769 |
| AAAA | 28 | | HIP | 55 | | | |
| LOC | 29 | | CDS | 59 | | | |
| SRV | 33 | | CDNSKEY | 60 | | | |
| NAPTR | 35 | | OPENPGPKEY | 61 | | | |
| KX | 36 | | | | | | |
| CERT | 37 | | | | | | |

Plain (non-flag) arguments that match a type name are treated as types:

  - `--class ANY` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "ANY"`
  - `--class 65536` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "65536"`
  - `--class XX` → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid query class "XX"`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""LOC rendering edge cases round 2."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

EQ = 2**31

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    # altitude fractions: -10.5m, 0.01m, 1.50m, -0.01m
    r.add_answer("a1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 - 1050))
    r.add_answer("a2.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 + 1))
    r.add_answer("a3.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 + 150))
    r.add_answer("a4.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 - 1))
    # size nibbles >= 10
    r.add_answer("sb.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0xAB, 0xCD, 0xEF, EQ, EQ, 10000000))
    # lat with min only, zero sec: 10 30 0 N; lon 5 0 0 E
    r.add_answer("m1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + (10*60+30)*60*1000, EQ + 5*3600*1000, 10000000))
    # exactly 1 second
    r.add_answer("m2.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + 1000, EQ - 1000, 10000000))
    # ms = 5 → 0.005
    r.add_answer("m3.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + 5, EQ + 50, 10000000))
    # ms = 500 → .500
    r.add_answer("m4.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + 59000 + 500, EQ + 500, 10000000))
    # max u32 lat/lon values (beyond 90/180 deg?)
    r.add_answer("x1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF))
    # zero lat/lon raw (most negative)
    r.add_answer("x2.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, 0, 0, 0))
    return r

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""LOC rendering edge cases round 2."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/probe")
from dnskit import *

EQ = 2**31

def handler(q):
    r = Response(q)
    # altitude fractions: -10.5m, 0.01m, 1.50m, -0.01m
    r.add_answer("a1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 - 1050))
    r.add_answer("a2.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 + 1))
    r.add_answer("a3.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 + 150))
    r.add_answer("a4.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, EQ, EQ, 10000000 - 1))
    # size nibbles >= 10
    r.add_answer("sb.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0xAB, 0xCD, 0xEF, EQ, EQ, 10000000))
    # lat with min only, zero sec: 10 30 0 N; lon 5 0 0 E
    r.add_answer("m1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + (10*60+30)*60*1000, EQ + 5*3600*1000, 10000000))
    # exactly 1 second
    r.add_answer("m2.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + 1000, EQ - 1000, 10000000))
    # ms = 5 → 0.005
    r.add_answer("m3.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + 5, EQ + 50, 10000000))
    # ms = 500 → .500
    r.add_answer("m4.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 EQ + 59000 + 500, EQ + 500, 10000000))
    # max u32 lat/lon values (beyond 90/180 deg?)
    r.add_answer("x1.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13,
                 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF))
    # zero lat/lon raw (most negative)
    r.add_answer("x2.example.com", "LOC", 60, LOC(0, 0x12, 0x16, 0x13, 0, 0, 0))
    return r

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(handler, port=int(sys.argv[1]))

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Spec written to `/workspace/specs/cli-args.md` (self-contained, ~370 lines, all commands/exit codes/verbatim messages/wire bytes included). Servers cleaned up.

**10-line summary of key findings:**

1. `--version` output has a literal stray `m` before the URL: `mhttps://dns.lookup.dog/` (114 bytes total; version is `v0.2.0-pre [d3a34280] built on 2026-04-17 (pre-release!)`); `-v`/`--version` and `-?`/`--help` all exit 0; `-h`/`-V` are unrecognized.
2. No-domain invocations (bare `dog`, `dog -1`, `dog A @ns`) print the full 1856-byte help to **stdout** with exit **3** — not an error message.
3. `-U -T` doesn't conflict: transports accumulate and one query per transport is sent in flag order; partial failure prints answer AND error, exit 1. Same flag twice (`-U -U`, `--time --time`) → `Option 'X' given more than once`.
4. `-H` with a non-URL nameserver **panics**: `thread 'main' (PID) panicked at dns-transport/src/https.rs:42:50: Invalid HTTPS nameserver`, exit 134 (SIGABRT).
5. Invalid `--color` values are silently ignored (treated as `automatic`); when both spellings given, `--color` always beats `--colour` regardless of order; `--color` greedily consumes the next token (`--color -1` eats `-1`).
6. Plain-arg guessing: `@…`→nameserver, case-insensitive known type (41 names incl. DLV/TA/EUI48/IXFR/ANY, but NOT DNSKEY/SVCB/HTTPS/SPF)→type, `IN/CH/HS`→class, **everything else**→domain (numbers, `::1`, `1.2.3.4`, `FOO` all become qnames); domains are lowercased and punycode-encoded on the wire.
7. `-q`/`-n` values bypass guessing literally: `-q @foo` queries qname `@foo`; `-n @127.0.0.1:…` fails OS lookup (`@` not stripped).
8. `--txid` accepts `0x` lowercase hex, `+N`, leading zeros (range 0–65535, one txid pins all queries); `-t`/`--class` accept decimal 0–65535 and `+1`/`01` but reject hex; nothing is whitespace-trimmed.
9. `--` stops option parsing but guessing still applies after it (`-- MX` is still a type); plain args starting with `-` → `Invalid domain "X"` exit 3.
10. All arg errors: stderr `dog: Invalid options: <msg>`, exit 3 (full verbatim catalog in spec, incl. special `OPT request is sent by default (see -Z flag)`); `-Z` takes one tweak each (`aa`/`ad`/`cd`/`bufsize=N` → flags 0x0400/0x0020/0x0010 + OPT payload), `--edns=disable` drops the OPT record, `hide`/`show` are wire-identical.

Spec complete at `/workspace/specs/query-wire.md`. Probe scripts left at `/workspace/probe/querywire_server.py` and `/workspace/probe/querywire_tc.py`; all servers killed, ports 5513–5519 free.

**10-line summary of key findings:**

1. Default UDP query: header `XXXX 0100 0001 0000 0000 0001` (RD only), one question, plus an EDNS OPT record `00 0029 0200 00000000 0000` — payload 512, version 0, flags 0 (no DO bit), empty rdata; 40 bytes total for `example.com`.
2. txid is fresh-random per query (never reused across a multi-query run); `--txid=N` (0–65535) forces that exact value on every query; out-of-range/non-numeric → `dog: Invalid options: Invalid transaction ID "N"`, exit 3.
3. `-Z` accepts exactly one tweak per flag occurrence (`-Z "aa ad"` is rejected): `aa`→flags 0x0500, `ad`→0x0120, `cd`→0x0110, `bufsize=N`→OPT class field (0–65535); combined `-Z aa -Z ad -Z cd` → 0x0530.
4. `--edns=disable` drops the OPT entirely (ARCOUNT=0); `hide` and `show` are wire-identical to default — and in this build OPT additionals in responses are never rendered in text or JSON under any setting.
5. 46 type names accepted (case-insensitive), all wire numbers enumerated; surprising: `DNSKEY`, `SVCB`, `HTTPS`, `SPF` rejected while `CDS/CDNSKEY/SMIMEA/OPENPGPKEY/TA/DLV` accepted; `-t OPT` gives a unique error message.
6. Bare numeric types AND classes are sent verbatim — even `-t 0` and `--class 0`/`--class 65535`; only >65535 or negative rejected.
7. Domains are lowercased and IDNA-punycode-encoded (`BÜCHER.DE` → `xn--bcher-kva.de`); trailing/leading dots stripped, empty labels collapsed (`a..b.com`→`a.b.com`); labels may not start/end with `-` (63-char limit per label) but spaces and underscores pass through raw; no 255-byte total-name limit enforced.
8. Querying a name in `/etc/hosts` (e.g. `localhost`) prints `warning: domain 'localhost.' also exists in hosts file` to stderr but still sends, exit 0; missing domain prints full help to stdout, exit 3.
9. Multiple domains/types/classes → cartesian product of separate single-question packets, ordered domain(outer)→type→class(inner), no dedup (`-t A -t A` sends twice).
10. TCP (`-T`): 2-byte big-endian length prefix + byte-identical payload, and a NEW TCP connection per query; on a TC=1 UDP response the default transport retries over TCP reusing the SAME txid, while `-U` does not retry and silently prints nothing with exit 0.
